title.zh: 卷三百十四 列傳第七十三 Fan Zhongyan and son: Chunyou, Chun Li, Chun Cui, Fan Chunren and son: Zhengping
title.raw: 卷三百十四 列傳第七十三 Fan Zhongyan and son: Chunyou, Chun Li, Chun Cui, Fan Chunren and son: Zhengping Volume 314 Biographies 73:

sentences.zh: 范仲淹

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan

sentences.zh: 范仲淹，字希文，唐宰相履冰之後。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan, styled Xiwen, was a descendant of the Tang chancellor Lü Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan, whose style name was Xiwen, was descended from the Tang chancellor Lü Bing.

sentences.zh: 其先邠州人也，後徙家江南，遂為蘇州吳縣人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were from Bin Prefecture; later the family moved to the south of the Yangtze and thus became natives of Wu County in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears came from Bin Prefecture; the family later relocated to the Jiangnan region and became established in Wu County, Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲淹二歲而孤，母更適長山朱氏，從其姓，名說。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was orphaned at age two; his mother remarried into the Zhu family of Changshan, and he took their surname and was named Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan lost his father when he was two. His mother married into the Zhu clan of Changshan, and the boy took their surname and was called Shuo.

sentences.zh: 少有志操，既長，知其世家，乃感泣辭母，去之應天府，依戚同文學。

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and integrity; when grown he learned of his patrician lineage, wept in emotion, took leave of his mother, went to Yingtian Prefecture, and studied under Qi Tongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed strong purpose and moral fiber. When he came of age and learned of his distinguished birth, he wept, bade his mother farewell, traveled to Yingtian Prefecture, and studied under Qi Tongwen.

sentences.zh: 晝夜不息，冬月憊甚，以水沃面；

translations.literal: Day and night he did not rest; in winter when utterly exhausted, he would splash water on his face;
translations.idiomatic: He studied without pause day and night; in the depths of winter, when fatigue overwhelmed him, he would splash cold water on his face;

sentences.zh: 食不給，至以糜粥繼之，人不能堪，仲淹不苦也。

translations.literal: food was insufficient, so that he had to sustain himself with thin gruel—others could not endure it, but Zhongyan did not find it bitter.
translations.idiomatic: when food ran short he lived on thin porridge. Others could not have borne such hardship, but Zhongyan never complained.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第，為廣德軍司理參軍，迎其母歸養。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed judicial assistant of Guangde Army, and brought his mother home to support her.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he became judicial assistant of Guangde Army and brought his mother home to live with him.

sentences.zh: 改集慶軍節度推官，始還姓，更其名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be investigating commissioner of Jiqing Army, at which time he first resumed his original surname and changed his given name.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made investigating commissioner of Jiqing Army; only then did he reclaim his birth surname and adopt the name by which he is known.

sentences.zh: 監泰州西溪鹽稅，遷大理寺丞，徙監楚州糧料院，母喪去官。

translations.literal: He supervised the Xixi salt tax in Taizhou, was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, was transferred to supervise the grain depot of Chuzhou, and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Xixi salt levy in Taizhou, rose to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then supervised Chuzhou's grain depot before resigning to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 晏殊知應天府，聞仲淹名，召寘府學。

translations.literal: Yan Shu was prefect of Yingtian Prefecture; hearing Zhongyan's reputation, he summoned him and placed him in the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Shu governed Yingtian Prefecture, he heard of Zhongyan's renown and appointed him to the prefectural academy.

sentences.zh: 上書請擇郡守，舉縣令，斥游惰，去冗僭，慎選舉，撫將帥，凡萬餘言。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting selection of prefects, promotion of county magistrates, dismissal of the idle and indolent, removal of superfluous ranks, careful conduct of examinations, and care for generals and commanders—in all more than ten thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne urging careful appointment of prefects and county magistrates, expulsion of the idle, elimination of redundant offices, stricter examinations, and better treatment of military commanders—a document of more than ten thousand characters in all.

sentences.zh: 服除，以殊薦，為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, on Yan Shu's recommendation he became collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was recommended by Yan Shu and appointed collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 仲淹泛通《六經》，長於《易》，學者多從質問，為執經講解，亡所倦。

translations.literal: Zhongyan had broad mastery of the Six Classics and excelled in the Book of Changes; many students came to question him, and he lectured on the classics without ever wearying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan had a wide command of the Six Classics and was especially skilled in the Book of Changes. Students flocked to him with questions, and he expounded the classics tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 嘗推其奉以食四方游士，諸子至易衣而出，仲淹晏如也。

translations.literal: He once used his salary to feed traveling scholars from all quarters; his sons had to change clothes before going out, yet Zhongyan remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He often devoted his official salary to feeding itinerant scholars from every region. His sons sometimes had to swap clothes before leaving the house, yet Zhongyan remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 每感激論天下事，奮不顧身，一時士大夫矯厲尚風節，自仲淹倡之。

translations.literal: Whenever moved he would discuss affairs of the realm, striving without regard for himself; for a time the scholar-officials cultivated stern integrity and prized moral conduct—this began with Zhongyan's advocacy.
translations.idiomatic: When stirred by events he would speak on national affairs with fearless passion. For a time the literati cultivated stern integrity and prized moral conduct—a trend that began with Zhongyan's example.

sentences.zh: 天聖七年，章獻太后將以冬至受朝，天子率百官上壽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tiansheng, Empress Dowager Zhangxian was to receive court on the winter solstice, and the emperor was to lead the hundred officials in offering birthday congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Tiansheng era, Empress Dowager Zhangxian planned to hold court on the winter solstice while the emperor led all officials in offering her birthday felicitations.

sentences.zh: 仲淹極言之，且曰：「奉親於內，自有家人禮，顧與百官同列，南面而朝之，不可為後世法。

translations.literal: Zhongyan spoke against it with utmost force, saying: "Serving one's parent within the palace has its own family rites; yet to stand in the same ranks as the hundred officials and face south to pay court to her—this cannot be a model for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan protested vehemently, saying, "Honoring a parent within the inner quarters follows household ritual. For the emperor to stand among the hundred officials and face south to pay court to her as a subject cannot become a precedent for later ages.

sentences.zh: 」且上疏請太后還政，不報。

translations.literal: " He also submitted a memorial requesting that the empress dowager return the government; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: " He also submitted a memorial asking the empress dowager to restore the government to the emperor, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 尋通判河中府，徙陳州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice prefect of Hezhong Prefecture, then transferred to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made vice prefect of Hezhong Prefecture, then transferred to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時方建太一宮及洪福院，市材木陝西。

translations.literal: At the time the Taiyi Palace and Hongfu Cloister were being built, and timber was being purchased in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Taiyi Palace and Hongfu Cloister were under construction, and timber was being procured from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 仲淹言：「昭應、壽寧，天戒不遠。

translations.literal: Zhongyan said: "The fires at Zhaoying and Shouning showed that Heaven's warning was not long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan said, "The fires at Zhaoying and Shouning showed that Heaven's warning came only recently.

sentences.zh: 今又侈土木，破民產，非所以順人心、合天意也。

translations.literal: Now again to lavish effort on buildings and timber, ruining the people's livelihood—this is not the way to accord with popular sentiment and Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: To lavish resources on construction again and ruin the people's livelihood is neither to win their hearts nor to align with Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 宜罷修寺觀，減常歲市木之數，以蠲除積負。

translations.literal: It is fitting to halt repair of temples and monasteries, reduce the annual quota for purchasing timber, and thereby remit accumulated debts.
translations.idiomatic: Construction of temples and monasteries should be halted, the annual timber purchases reduced, and accumulated debts forgiven.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「恩幸多以內降除官，非太平之政。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Favored intimates are too often appointed to office by inner edict—this is not government befitting an age of peace.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Favored courtiers too often receive appointments through private edicts from within the palace—hardly the policy of a tranquil age.

sentences.zh: 」事雖不行，仁宗以為忠。

translations.literal: " Though his proposals were not adopted, Renzong regarded him as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: " Though his proposals were not adopted, Emperor Renzong considered him loyal.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，召為右司諫。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, he was summoned as remonstrating secretary of the right bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death he was summoned to serve as remonstrating secretary of the right bureau.

sentences.zh: 言事者多暴太后時事，仲淹曰：「太后受遺先帝，調護陛下者十餘年，宜掩其小故，以全后德。

translations.literal: Many who spoke on affairs exposed matters from the empress dowager's regency; Zhongyan said: "The empress dowager received the late emperor's testamentary charge and nurtured Your Majesty for more than ten years—her minor faults should be covered to preserve the empress dowager's virtue in full.
translations.idiomatic: Many memorialists dredged up affairs from the regency. Zhongyan said, "The empress dowager received the late emperor's dying charge and guided Your Majesty for more than ten years. Her minor faults should be overlooked so that her virtue may stand complete.

sentences.zh: 」帝為詔中外，毋輒論太后時事。

translations.literal: " The emperor issued an edict to court and realm that none should rashly discuss affairs of the empress dowager's regency.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then issued an edict forbidding officials throughout the empire to discuss the regency without cause.

sentences.zh: 初，太后遺誥乙太妃楊氏為皇太后，參決軍國事。

translations.literal: Earlier, the empress dowager's testamentary edict had elevated Consort Yang to empress dowager with participation in military and state decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the late empress dowager's testament had elevated Consort Yang to empress dowager with authority to participate in military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 仲淹曰：「太后，母號也，自古無因保育而代立者。

translations.literal: Zhongyan said: "Empress dowager is a title of mother; since antiquity there has never been one who, merely for having nursed and reared the ruler, was installed to rule in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan said, "Empress dowager is a title reserved for a mother. Never in history has someone been elevated to rule merely for having nursed and raised the emperor.

sentences.zh: 今一太后崩，又立一太后，天下且疑陛下不可一日無母后之助矣。」

translations.literal: Now one empress dowager has died and another is installed—the realm will suspect that Your Majesty cannot go a single day without a empress dowager's assistance."
translations.idiomatic: Now one empress dowager has just died and another is installed—the realm will suspect that Your Majesty cannot govern for a single day without a empress dowager at your side."

sentences.zh: 歲大蝗旱，江、淮、京東滋甚。

translations.literal: That year locusts and drought were severe; along the Yangtze, Huai, and Jingdong circuits the suffering grew extreme.
translations.idiomatic: That year locusts and drought struck hard, with the Yangtze, Huai, and Jingdong regions suffering most severely.

sentences.zh: 仲淹請遣使循行，未報。

translations.literal: Zhongyan requested that envoys be sent to tour the affected areas; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan asked that envoys be dispatched to inspect the stricken regions, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 乃請間曰：「宮掖中半日不食，當何如？

translations.literal: He then requested a private audience and said: "If those within the palace went half a day without food, what then?
translations.idiomatic: He then sought a private audience and asked, "If those within the palace went half a day without food, what would that mean?

sentences.zh: 」帝側然，乃命仲淹安撫江、淮，所至開倉振之，且禁民淫祀，奏蠲廬舒折役茶、江東丁口鹽錢，且條上救弊十事。

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved; he then ordered Zhongyan to pacify the Jianghuai region. Wherever he went he opened granaries for relief, forbade improper popular sacrifices, memorialized remission of the Lu-Shu tea levy in commuted labor and the Jiangdong head-tax salt levy, and submitted ten items for remedying abuses.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply moved and appointed Zhongyan to pacify the Jianghuai region. Wherever he went he opened granaries for relief, banned improper popular sacrifices, memorialized remission of the Lu-Shu tea levy in commuted labor and the Jiangdong head-tax salt levy, and submitted ten proposals for remedying abuses.

sentences.zh: 會郭皇后廢，率諫官、御史伏閣爭之，不能得。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed, he led remonstrating officials and censors to prostrate themselves at the palace gate in protest, but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo was deposed, he led remonstrating officials and censors to kneel at the palace gate in protest, but they could not change the decision.

sentences.zh: 明日，將留百官揖宰相廷爭，方至待漏院，有詔出知睦州。

translations.literal: The next day, intending to detain the hundred officials to bow to the chief councilor and dispute the matter in court, he had just reached the dawn-waiting courtyard when an edict came appointing him prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, planning to keep the officials at court to confront the chief councilor, he had just reached the dawn-waiting courtyard when an edict arrived appointing him prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徙蘇州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 州大水，民田不得耕，仲淹疏五河，導太湖注之海，募人興作，未就，尋徙明州，轉運使奏留仲淹以畢其役，許之。

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered great flood; the people's fields could not be cultivated. Zhongyan dredged five rivers, channeling Lake Tai into the sea, and recruited labor for the work. Before completion he was soon transferred to Ming Prefecture; the transport commissioner memorialized to retain Zhongyan to finish the project, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: A great flood inundated the prefecture and left the fields untilled. Zhongyan dredged five rivers to channel Lake Tai's waters to the sea and recruited labor for the project. Before it was finished he was transferred to Ming Prefecture, but the transport commissioner asked that Zhongyan be kept on to complete the work, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書禮部員外郎、天章閣待制，召還，判國子監，遷吏部員外郎、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat and academician awaiting orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion, recalled to court, made administrator of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel with acting authority over Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites and academician awaiting orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion, recalled to the capital, put in charge of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel with acting authority over Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時呂夷簡執政，進用者多出其門。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Yijian held power; most of those advanced to office came from his faction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lü Yijian dominated the government, and most promotions came from his circle.

sentences.zh: 仲淹上《百官圖》，指其次第曰：「如此為序遷，如此為不次，如此則公，如此則私。

translations.literal: Zhongyan submitted the "Chart of the Hundred Officials," pointing to the gradations and saying: "Thus is orderly advancement; thus is irregular promotion; thus is public; thus is private.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan submitted his Chart of the Hundred Officials, indicating each rank in turn: "This is orderly advancement; this is irregular promotion; this serves the public good; this serves private interest.

sentences.zh: 況進退近臣，凡超格者，不宜全委之宰相。

translations.literal: Moreover, in advancing and retiring close ministers, all who exceed the norm should not be wholly entrusted to the chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, promotions and dismissals of close ministers that exceed normal procedure should not be left entirely to the chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 」夷簡不悅。

translations.literal: " Yijian was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Yijian was displeased.

sentences.zh: 他日，論建都之事，仲淹曰：「洛陽險固，而汴為四戰之地，太平宜居汴，即有事必居洛陽。

translations.literal: On another day, discussing the choice of capital, Zhongyan said: "Luoyang is secure by terrain, whereas Bian is a place contested on four sides. In peace Bian is suitable for residence; if trouble arises one must reside at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, discussing the capital, Zhongyan said, "Luoyang is secure by terrain, whereas Bian lies in a region fought over from every direction. In peace the court should remain at Bian; if trouble comes it must move to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 當漸廣儲蓄，繕宮室。

translations.literal: One should gradually expand stores and repair the palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Stores should be expanded gradually and the palaces at Luoyang maintained in readiness.

sentences.zh: 」帝問夷簡，夷簡曰：「此仲淹迂闊之論也。

translations.literal: " The emperor asked Yijian, who said: "This is Zhongyan's impractical and far-fetched talk.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked Yijian, who replied, "This is Zhongyan's impractical, wide-ranging talk.

sentences.zh: 」仲淹乃為四論以獻，大抵譏切時政。

translations.literal: " Zhongyan then composed four treatises and presented them, mostly satirizing and criticizing current policy.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongyan then wrote four treatises for the throne, mostly sharp critiques of current policy.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「漢成帝信張禹，不疑舅家，故有新莽之禍。

translations.literal: He also said: "Emperor Cheng of Han trusted Zhang Yu and did not doubt his mother's kin, and thus came the disaster of Wang Mang.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Emperor Cheng of Han trusted Zhang Yu and never doubted his maternal relatives, and thus Wang Mang's catastrophe followed.

sentences.zh: 臣恐今日亦有張禹，壞陛下家法。

translations.literal: I fear that today too there may be a Zhang Yu who will ruin Your Majesty's household norms.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that today as well there may be a Zhang Yu who will undermine Your Majesty's household discipline.

sentences.zh: 」夷簡怒訴曰：「仲淹離間陛下君臣，所引用，皆朋黨也。

translations.literal: " Yijian angrily complained: "Zhongyan is driving a wedge between Your Majesty and your ministers; those he recommends are all a faction.
translations.idiomatic: " Yijian angrily protested, "Zhongyan is driving a wedge between Your Majesty and your ministers. Everyone he recommends belongs to a faction.

sentences.zh: 」仲淹對益切，由是罷知饒州。

translations.literal: " Zhongyan's replies grew still sharper; thereby he was dismissed and made prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongyan's replies grew even sharper, and he was dismissed to serve as prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史韓瀆希宰相旨，請書仲淹朋黨，揭之朝堂。

translations.literal: Palace censor Han Du, courting the chief councilor's intent, requested that Zhongyan's faction be written out and posted in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Han Du, eager to please the chief councilor, asked that the names of Zhongyan's faction be written out and posted in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 於是秘書丞余靖上言曰：「仲淹以一言忤宰相，遽加貶竄，況前所言者在陛下母子夫婦之間乎？

translations.literal: Thereupon secretary Yu Jing submitted a statement: "Zhongyan, for a single remark that offended the chief councilor, was suddenly demoted and banished—how much more when his earlier words concerned matters between Your Majesty as mother and son and as husband and wife?
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Yu Jing then memorialized, "Zhongyan was suddenly demoted and banished for a single remark that offended the chief councilor—yet his earlier words concerned the most intimate relations between mother and son and between husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 陛下既優容之矣，臣請追改前命。

translations.literal: Your Majesty already showed him forbearance; I request that the previous order be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already showed him forbearance then. I ask that the previous order be reversed.

sentences.zh: 」太子中允尹洙自訟與仲淹師友，且嘗薦己，願從降黜。

translations.literal: " Crown prince attendant Yin Zhu pleaded that he was Zhongyan's teacher and friend and had once recommended himself, and wished to share in demotion.
translations.idiomatic: " Crown prince attendant Yin Zhu declared that he was Zhongyan's teacher and friend, that Zhongyan had once recommended him, and that he wished to share in the demotion.

sentences.zh: 館閣校勘歐陽修以高若訥在諫官，坐視而不言，移書責之。

translations.literal: Archive collator Ouyang Xiu, because Gao Ruonu held a remonstrance post yet sat by and did not speak, sent him a letter reproaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Archive collator Ouyang Xiu, seeing that Gao Ruonu held a remonstrance post yet remained silent, sent him a letter of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 由是，三人者偕坐貶。

translations.literal: Thereby all three were punished with demotion together.
translations.idiomatic: As a result all three were demoted together.

sentences.zh: 明年，夷簡亦罷，自是朋黨之論興矣。

translations.literal: The next year Yijian too was dismissed; from this the talk of factions arose.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yijian was dismissed as well, and from that time talk of factions spread through the court.

sentences.zh: 仲淹既去，士大夫為論薦者不已。

translations.literal: After Zhongyan departed, the scholar-officials never ceased recommending him in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyan left office, scholar-officials never ceased speaking in his favor.

sentences.zh: 仁宗謂宰相張士遜曰：「向貶仲淹，為其密請建立皇太弟故也。

translations.literal: Renzong said to Chief Councilor Zhang Shisun: "The earlier demotion of Zhongyan was because he secretly requested the establishment of a grand imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong told Chief Councilor Zhang Shisun, "I demoted Zhongyan earlier because he had secretly urged the establishment of a grand imperial younger brother.

sentences.zh: 今朋黨稱薦如此，奈何？

translations.literal: Now the faction praises and recommends him thus—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Now his faction praises and recommends him so insistently—what can be done?

sentences.zh: 」再下詔戒敕。

translations.literal: " Edicts of admonition were again issued.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued further edicts of warning.

sentences.zh: 仲淹在饒州歲餘，徙潤州，又徙越州。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was at Raozhou for more than a year, was transferred to Run Prefecture, then again to Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan spent a little more than a year at Raozhou, then was transferred to Run Prefecture and later to Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，召為天章閣待制、知永興軍，改陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was summoned as academician awaiting orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion and military commissioner of Yongxing Army, then made metropolitan transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled, Zhongyan was recalled as academician awaiting orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion and commissioner of Yongxing Army, then appointed metropolitan transport commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 會夏竦為陝西經略安撫、招討使，進仲淹龍圖閣直學士以副之。

translations.literal: When Xia Song became pacification and repression commissioner of Shaanxi, Zhongyan was advanced to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Song was made pacification and repression commissioner for Shaanxi, Zhongyan was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion to serve as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 夷簡再入相，帝諭仲淹使釋前憾。

translations.literal: Yijian again entered the chief councilorship; the emperor instructed Zhongyan to release former resentments.
translations.idiomatic: When Yijian returned to the chief councilorship, the emperor urged Zhongyan to set aside their old grievances.

sentences.zh: 仲淹頓首謝曰：「臣鄉論蓋國家事，于夷簡無憾也。」

translations.literal: Zhongyan bowed his head and replied: "My rustic opinions concerned affairs of the state; toward Yijian I bear no resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan bowed low and replied, "My blunt words concerned affairs of state alone. I bear no personal resentment toward Yijian."

sentences.zh: 延州諸砦多失守，仲淹自請行，遷戶部郎中兼知延州。

translations.literal: Many forts of Yan Prefecture had been lost; Zhongyan volunteered to go, was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent authority as prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Many forts around Yan Prefecture had fallen. Zhongyan volunteered to take the field and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent appointment as prefect of Yan.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔分邊兵：總管領萬人，鈐轄領五千人，都監領三千人。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had divided border troops: the overall commander led ten thousand, the deputy commander five thousand, and the supervisory commissioner three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had divided the border forces so that the overall commander led ten thousand men, the deputy commander five thousand, and the supervisory commissioner three thousand.

sentences.zh: 寇至禦之，則官卑者先出。

translations.literal: When bandits came to be resisted, the lower in rank went out first.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy attacked, the lower-ranking officer had to lead out first.

sentences.zh: 仲淹曰：「將不擇人，以官為先後，取敗之道也。

translations.literal: Zhongyan said: "Not to choose generals but to order them by rank—this is the way to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan said, "To send commanders into battle in order of rank rather than ability is a recipe for defeat.

sentences.zh: 」於是大閱州兵，得萬八千人，分為六，各將三千人，分部教之，量賊眾寡，使更出禦賊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he held a great review of the prefectural troops, obtained eighteen thousand, divided them into six groups of three thousand each under separate commanders, trained them by division, gauged the enemy's numbers, and had them rotate in going out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: " He then held a grand review of the prefectural troops, mustered eighteen thousand men, divided them into six brigades of three thousand under separate commanders, trained each unit, and sent them out in rotation according to the size of the enemy force.

sentences.zh: 時塞門、承平諸砦既廢，用種世衡策，城青澗以據賊沖，大興營田，且聽民得互市，以通有無。

translations.literal: At the time the forts of Saimen and Chengping had been abandoned; adopting Zhong Shihang's plan, he walled Qingjian to hold the enemy's route of attack, greatly expanded military colonies, and permitted the people to trade across the border to exchange what they had and lacked.
translations.idiomatic: The forts of Saimen and Chengping had been abandoned. Following Zhong Shihang's plan, he fortified Qingjian to block the enemy's main approach, greatly expanded military farming, and allowed border trade so goods could flow between the two sides.

sentences.zh: 又以民遠輸勞苦，請建鄜城為軍，以河中、同、華中下戶稅租就輸之。

translations.literal: Also, because the people suffered from long-distance transport, he requested that Fucheng be made an army command so that the tax grain of lower households in Hezhong, Tong, and Huazhong could be delivered nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Because long-distance transport exhausted the people, he asked that Fucheng be made an army command so that tax grain from lower households in Hezhong, Tong, and Huazhong could be delivered locally.

sentences.zh: 春夏徙兵就食，可省糴十之三，他所減不與。

translations.literal: Moving troops in spring and summer to where food was available could save three-tenths of grain purchases—reductions elsewhere did not match this.
translations.idiomatic: Moving troops in spring and summer to where provisions were available could save thirty percent on grain purchases—savings nowhere else matched this.

sentences.zh: 詔以為康定軍。

translations.literal: An edict established it as the Kangding Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established the Kangding Army there.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，詔諸路入討，仲淹曰：「正月塞外大寒，我師暴露，不如俟春深入，賊馬瘦人饑，勢易制也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year an edict ordered all circuits to advance in punitive campaign. Zhongyan said: "In the first month beyond the passes the cold is extreme; our army would be exposed—better to wait until spring for a deep advance, when the enemy's horses are lean and men hungry and they are easier to control.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year an edict ordered all circuits to launch a punitive campaign. Zhongyan said, "Beyond the passes in the first month the cold is extreme and our troops would suffer exposure. Better to wait until spring for a deep advance, when the enemy's horses are lean, their men hungry, and they easier to overcome.

sentences.zh: 況邊備漸修，師出有紀，賊雖猖獗，固已懾其氣矣。

translations.literal: Moreover border defenses are gradually improved and troops move out with discipline; though the enemy is fierce, their spirit is already cowed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, border defenses are steadily improving and our forces now march with discipline. However fierce the enemy may seem, their spirit is already shaken.

sentences.zh: 鄜、延密邇靈、夏，西羌必由之地也。

translations.literal: Fu and Yan lie close to Ling and Xia—the Western Qiang must pass through this region.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Yan lie close to Ling and Xia—the Western Qiang must pass through this region.

sentences.zh: 第按兵不動，以觀其釁，許臣稍以恩信招來之。

translations.literal: Simply hold the army still and watch for openings; allow me gradually to win them over with kindness and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Simply hold our forces in place and watch for an opening. Allow me gradually to win them over with kindness and good faith.

sentences.zh: 不然，情意阻絕，臣恐偃兵無期矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, with feeling and intent cut off, I fear there will be no end to the halting of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, once goodwill is severed, I fear peace will never come.

sentences.zh: 若臣策不效，當舉兵先取綏、宥，據要害，屯兵營田，為持久計，則茶山、橫山之民，必挈族來歸矣。

translations.literal: If my plan does not succeed, we should raise troops first to take Sui and You, hold the strategic points, station troops and open military colonies as a long-term plan—then the people of Chashan and Hengshan will surely bring their clans to submit.
translations.idiomatic: If my plan fails, we should raise troops to seize Sui and You first, hold the strategic points, garrison troops, and open military colonies for a long campaign. Then the people of Chashan and Hengshan will surely bring their families over to our side.

sentences.zh: 拓疆禦寇，策之上也。

translations.literal: Expanding territory to repel invaders is the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Expanding our territory to hold off the enemy is the best strategy of all.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆用其議。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor adopted all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 仲淹又請修承平、永平等砦，稍招還流亡，定堡障，通斥候，城十二砦，於是羌漢之民，相踵歸業。

translations.literal: Zhongyan also requested repair of the forts Chengping and Yongping, gradual recall of exiles, fixing of fortifications and barriers, opening of scouts and lookouts, and building twelve forts; thereby Qiang and Han people returned to their occupations one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan also asked to rebuild the forts at Chengping and Yongping, gradually recall exiles, secure the border defenses, restore scouting networks, and construct twelve new forts. Qiang and Han people then returned to their farms in steady streams.

sentences.zh: 久之，元昊歸陷將高延德，因與仲淹約和，仲淹為書戒喻之。

translations.literal: After a long time Yuanhao returned the captured general Gao Yande and thereby made peace overtures to Zhongyan; Zhongyan wrote a letter admonishing and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Yuanhao returned the captured general Gao Yande and opened peace talks with Zhongyan, who wrote him a letter of admonition and counsel.

sentences.zh: 會任福敗于好水川，元昊答書語不遜，仲淹對來使焚之。

translations.literal: When Ren Fu was defeated at Hao River, Yuanhao's reply letter used insolent language; Zhongyan burned it before the envoy who had brought it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Fu was defeated at Hao River, Yuanhao's reply used insolent language. Zhongyan burned the letter in front of the envoy who had brought it.

sentences.zh: 大臣以為不當輒通書，又不當輒焚之，宋庠請斬仲淹，帝不聽。

translations.literal: The great ministers held that he should not have exchanged letters rashly, nor burned them rashly; Song Kui requested that Zhongyan be executed, but the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers held that he should not have exchanged letters so freely or burned them so readily. Song Kui asked that Zhongyan be executed, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 降本曹員外郎、知耀州，徙慶州，遷左司郎中，為環慶路經略安撫、緣邊招討使。

translations.literal: He was demoted to vice director of his original bureau and made prefect of Yao Prefecture, transferred to Qing Prefecture, promoted to director of the left bureau, and made pacification commissioner of Huanqing Circuit and border repression commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to vice director of his former bureau and appointed prefect of Yao Prefecture, then transferred to Qing Prefecture, promoted to director of the left bureau, and made pacification commissioner of Huanqing Circuit with authority as border repression commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，元昊反，陰誘屬羌為助，而環慶酋長六百余人，約為鄉道'事尋露。

translations.literal: Initially when Yuanhao rebelled, he secretly enticed dependent Qiang to assist him; more than six hundred chieftains of Huanqing had agreed to act as guides, but the matter was soon exposed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao first rebelled, he secretly won dependent Qiang tribes to his side. More than six hundred chieftains of Huanqing had agreed to serve as guides, but the plot was soon exposed.

sentences.zh: 仲淹以其反復不常也，至部即奏行邊，以詔書犒賞諸羌，閱其人馬，為立條約：「若仇已和斷，輒私報之及傷人者，罰羊百、馬二，已殺者斬。

translations.literal: Zhongyan, because they were inconstant in shifting sides, upon reaching his post immediately memorialized to tour the border, used an imperial edict to reward the various Qiang, reviewed their men and horses, and established regulations: "If enmity has already been settled and peace concluded, yet one privately takes revenge or injures a person, the penalty is one hundred sheep and two horses; if already killed, execution.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their tendency to switch sides, Zhongyan memorialized as soon as he took office to tour the border, rewarded the Qiang tribes by imperial edict, inspected their men and horses, and established regulations: "If a feud has been settled and someone still takes private revenge or injures another, the penalty is one hundred sheep and two horses; if the victim has been killed, the offender is executed.

sentences.zh: 負債爭訟，聽告官為理，輒質縛平人者，罰羊五十、馬一。

translations.literal: For debt disputes and lawsuits, they may report to officials for judgment; if one rashly seizes and binds an ordinary person as hostage, the penalty is fifty sheep and one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Debt disputes and lawsuits must be brought to officials for judgment. Anyone who seizes and binds an ordinary person as hostage is fined fifty sheep and one horse.

sentences.zh: 賊馬入界，追集不赴隨本族，每戶罰羊二，質其首領。

translations.literal: When enemy horses enter the border, if upon summons one does not assemble and follow one's tribe, each household is fined two sheep and the chieftain is held as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy horsemen cross the border, any household that fails to muster with its tribe when summoned is fined two sheep per household, and the chieftain is held as hostage.

sentences.zh: 賊大入，老幼入保本砦，官為給食；

translations.literal: When the enemy enters in force, the old and young enter their tribe's protective fort and the government provides food;
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy raids in force, the old and young enter their tribe's protective fort and the government provides food;

sentences.zh: 即不入砦，本家罰羊二；

translations.literal: if they do not enter the fort, that household is fined two sheep;
translations.idiomatic: if they fail to enter the fort, that household is fined two sheep;

sentences.zh: 全族不至，質其首領。

translations.literal: if the whole clan does not come, the chieftain is held as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: if the entire clan fails to come, the chieftain is held as hostage.

sentences.zh: 」諸羌皆受命，自是始為漢用矣。

translations.literal: " All the Qiang accepted the orders; from this time they began to serve the Han.
translations.idiomatic: " All the Qiang accepted these terms, and from that time they began to serve the Song.

sentences.zh: 改邠州觀察使，仲淹表言：「觀察使班待制下，臣守邊數年，羌人頗親愛臣，呼臣為'龍圖老子'。

translations.literal: He was made observation commissioner of Bin Prefecture; Zhongyan submitted a memorial saying: "The observation commissioner ranks below an academician awaiting orders; I have guarded the border for several years and the Qiang are quite fond of me, calling me 'Old Man Longtu.'
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Bin Prefecture. Zhongyan memorialized, "The observation commissioner ranks below an academician awaiting orders, yet I have guarded the border for several years and the Qiang have grown fond of me, calling me 'Old Man Longtu.'

sentences.zh: 今退而與王興、朱觀為伍，第恐為賊輕矣。

translations.literal: If I now step back and am grouped with Wang Xing and Zhu Guan, I only fear the enemy will hold us in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: If I now step back to join Wang Xing and Zhu Guan in rank, I fear the enemy will only hold us in contempt.

sentences.zh: 」辭不拜。

translations.literal: He declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the appointment and refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 慶之西北馬鋪砦，當後橋川口，在賊腹中。

translations.literal: Northwest of Qing Prefecture was Mapu Fort, situated at the mouth of Houqiao Stream, deep within enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Mapu Fort lay northwest of Qing Prefecture, at the mouth of Houqiao Stream—squarely in the heart of enemy-held land.

sentences.zh: 仲淹欲城之，度賊必爭，密遣子純祐與蕃將趙明先據其地，引兵隨之。

translations.literal: Zhongyan wished to fortify it; reckoning the enemy would certainly contest it, he secretly sent his son Chunyou and the tribal general Zhao Ming to seize the ground first, then led troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan wanted to build a fort there. Expecting the enemy would fight for the site, he secretly sent his son Chunyou and the tribal officer Zhao Ming to occupy it first, then marched troops up after them.

sentences.zh: 諸將不知所向，行至柔遠，始號令之，版築皆具，旬日而城成，即大順城是也。

translations.literal: The generals did not know where they were headed; only when they reached Rouyuan did he finally issue orders. All materials for wall-building were prepared, and in ten days the fort was complete—this was Dazhun Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had no idea where they were going until, at Rouyuan, Zhongyan finally issued his orders. Building materials were already on hand, and within ten days the fort was finished—this became Dazhun Fort.

sentences.zh: 賊覺，以騎三萬來戰，佯北，仲淹戒勿追，已而果有伏。

translations.literal: The enemy detected it and came to fight with thirty thousand cavalry, feigning retreat. Zhongyan warned against pursuit, and afterward there indeed proved to be an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy discovered the move and attacked with thirty thousand horsemen, feigning retreat. Zhongyan warned his men not to pursue—and soon enough a hidden force appeared.

sentences.zh: 大順既城，而白豹、金湯皆不敢犯，環慶自此寇益少。

translations.literal: Once Dazhun was fortified, even Baibao and Jintang dared not invade, and from then on raids in Huanqing grew fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dazhun was fortified, the enemy did not dare attack from Baibao or Jintang, and incursions into Huanqing grew steadily fewer.

sentences.zh: 明珠、滅臧勁兵數萬，仲淹聞涇原欲襲討之，上言曰：「二族道險，不可攻，前日高繼嵩已喪師。

translations.literal: Mingzhu and Miezang had tens of thousands of crack troops. Zhongyan heard that Jingyuan Circuit intended to strike and subdue them and submitted a memorial saying: "The two tribes occupy difficult terrain and cannot be attacked; previously Gao Jisong already lost his army.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingzhu and Miezang tribes fielded tens of thousands of elite warriors. When Zhongyan learned that Jingyuan Circuit planned to attack them, he memorialized: "These two tribes hold rugged territory that cannot be taken by force—Gao Jisong already lost his army there.

sentences.zh: 平時且懷反側，今討之，必與賊表裏，南入原州，西擾鎮戎，東侵環州，邊患未艾也。

translations.literal: Even in normal times they nurse divided loyalties; if we attack them now, they will surely coordinate with the enemy inside and out—driving south into Yuan Prefecture, harassing Zhenrong in the west, and invading Huan Prefecture in the east; border troubles will never end.
translations.idiomatic: Even in peacetime their loyalty is doubtful. An attack now would surely drive them to collude with the enemy—striking south into Yuan Prefecture, raiding Zhenrong in the west, and pressing Huan Prefecture in the east. The border would never know peace.

sentences.zh: 若北取細腰、胡蘆眾泉為堡障，以斷賊路，則二族安，而環州、鎮戎徑道通徹，可無憂矣。

translations.literal: If we instead take Xiyao, Hulu, and the many springs to the north as fortifications to cut the enemy's routes, the two tribes will be secure, and the direct roads to Huan and Zhenrong will be fully open—then we need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: If we instead seize Xiyao, Hulu, and the other springs to the north and fortify them to block enemy routes, the two tribes will remain loyal and the main roads to Huan and Zhenrong will stay open—we would have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」其後，遂築細腰、胡蘆諸砦。

translations.literal: Thereafter, Xiyao, Hulu, and the other forts were built.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the forts at Xiyao, Hulu, and elsewhere were constructed as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 葛懷敏敗於定川，賊大掠至潘原，關中震恐，民多竄山谷間。

translations.literal: Ge Huaimin was defeated at Dingchuan; the enemy pillaged on a great scale as far as Panyuan. Guanzhong shook with terror, and many people fled into mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Huaimin was routed at Dingchuan, the enemy plundered all the way to Panyuan. Terror spread through Guanzhong, and countless people hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 仲淹率眾六千，由邠、涇援之，聞賊已出塞，乃還。

translations.literal: Zhongyan led six thousand men to their relief by way of Bin and Jing, but on hearing the enemy had already withdrawn beyond the frontier, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan marched six thousand men through Bin and Jing to their aid, but when he learned the enemy had already withdrawn beyond the passes, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 始，定川事聞，帝按圖謂左右曰：「若仲淹出援，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: At first, when word of Dingchuan reached the emperor, he spread a map and said to those around him: "If Zhongyan goes out to aid them, I need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Dingchuan first arrived, the emperor spread a map before his attendants and said, "If Zhongyan marches to their relief, I shall have no cause for worry.

sentences.zh: 」奏至，帝大喜曰：「吾固知仲淹可用也。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor rejoiced greatly and said: "I always knew Zhongyan could be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the emperor was delighted: "I always knew Zhongyan was the man for this.

sentences.zh: 」進樞密直學士、右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician of the Privy Council and right remonstrance grand master.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was promoted to academician of the Privy Council and Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 仲淹以軍出無功，辭不敢受命，詔不聽。

translations.literal: Zhongyan, because the army had sortied without achievement, declined and dared not accept; an edict refused to hear him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan declined the honors, saying his relief column had achieved nothing; the throne would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 時已命文彥博經略涇原，帝以涇原傷夷，欲對徙仲淹，遣王懷德喻之。

translations.literal: At the time Wen Yanbo had already been appointed to oversee Jingyuan Circuit. Because Jingyuan had suffered heavy losses, the emperor wished to transfer Zhongyan in exchange and sent Wang Huade to explain this to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo had already been assigned to oversee Jingyuan Circuit. Seeing how badly Jingyuan had been mauled, the emperor wanted to swap Zhongyan into the post and sent Wang Huade to sound him out.

sentences.zh: 仲淹謝曰：「涇原地重，第恐臣不足當此路。

translations.literal: Zhongyan declined, saying: "Jingyuan Circuit is weighty ground; I only fear I am not equal to this command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan declined: "Jingyuan Circuit is critical territory—I fear I am not up to holding that line.

sentences.zh: 與韓琦同經略涇原，並駐涇州，琦兼秦鳳、臣兼環慶。

translations.literal: Let me jointly oversee Jingyuan Circuit with Han Qi, both stationed at Jing Prefecture—Qi also holding Qin and Feng, and I also holding Huan and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Let Han Qi and I jointly oversee Jingyuan, both based at Jing Prefecture—he covering Qin and Feng while I cover Huan and Qing.

sentences.zh: 涇原有警，臣與韓琦合秦鳳，環慶之兵，掎角而進；

translations.literal: If Jingyuan is alarmed, Han Qi and I will combine the forces of Qin-Feng and Huan-Qing and advance in mutual support;
translations.idiomatic: If Jingyuan comes under attack, Han Qi and I will unite the armies of Qin-Feng and Huan-Qing and advance in concert;

sentences.zh: 若秦鳳、環慶有警，亦可率涇原之師為援。

translations.literal: if Qin-Feng or Huan-Qing is alarmed, we may likewise lead the armies of Jingyuan as relief.
translations.idiomatic: if Qin-Feng or Huan-Qing is threatened, we can march Jingyuan troops to their aid.

sentences.zh: 臣當與琦練兵選將，漸復橫山，以斷賊臂，不數年間，可期平定矣。

translations.literal: I and Qi should drill troops and select generals, gradually recover Hengshan, and sever the enemy's arm; within a few years, pacification may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and I should train troops, pick commanders, and gradually win back Hengshan—cutting off the enemy's reach. Within a few years we could bring the frontier to order.

sentences.zh: 願詔龐籍兼領環慶，以成首尾之勢。

translations.literal: I ask that Pang Ji be ordered to also command Huan and Qing, so as to complete a head-and-tail disposition.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Pang Ji be assigned to command Huan and Qing as well, linking both ends of the line.

sentences.zh: 秦州委文彥博，慶州用滕宗諒總之。

translations.literal: Qin Prefecture should be entrusted to Wen Yanbo; Qing Prefecture should be overseen by Teng Zongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Leave Qin Prefecture to Wen Yanbo and place Qing Prefecture under Teng Zongliang.

sentences.zh: 孫沔亦可辦集。

translations.literal: Sun Mian can also manage the muster.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian can handle supply and assembly.

sentences.zh: 渭州，一武臣足矣。

translations.literal: For Wei Prefecture, one military officer is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prefecture needs only a single seasoned military officer.

sentences.zh: 」帝採用其言，復置陝西路安撫、經略、招討使，以仲淹、韓琦、龐籍分領之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his words, restored the posts of pacification commissioner, frontier commissioner, and campaign commander for Shaanxi Circuit, and had Zhongyan, Han Qi, and Pang Ji divide command among them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his plan, restored the Shaanxi frontier posts of pacification, military oversight, and campaign command, and divided responsibility among Zhongyan, Han Qi, and Pang Ji.

sentences.zh: 仲淹與琦開府涇州，而徙彥博帥秦，宗諒帥慶，張亢帥渭。

translations.literal: Zhongyan and Qi opened their headquarters at Jing Prefecture, while Yanbo was moved to command Qin, Zongliang to command Qing, and Zhang Kang to command Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan and Han Qi established headquarters at Jing Prefecture while Yanbo took command of Qin, Zongliang of Qing, and Zhang Kang of Wei.

sentences.zh: 仲淹為將，號令明白，愛撫士卒，諸羌來者，推心接之不疑，故賊亦不敢輒犯其境。

translations.literal: As a general, Zhongyan's orders were clear, he cherished and comforted his soldiers, and toward Qiang who came to him he received them with open trust without suspicion; therefore the enemy also did not dare lightly violate his territory.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Zhongyan gave clear orders and treated his men with genuine care. Qiang who came to him he met with open-handed trust—and because of that, the enemy scarcely dared cross his borders.

sentences.zh: 元昊請和，召拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao sued for peace, Zhongyan was summoned and appointed vice commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao sought peace, Zhongyan was recalled and made Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 王舉正懦默不任事，諫官歐陽修等言仲淹有相材，請罷舉正用仲淹，遂改參知政事。

translations.literal: Wang Juzheng was timid and silent and unsuited to duty. Remonstrance officials including Ouyang Xiu said Zhongyan had the talent of a chief minister and asked that Juzheng be removed and Zhongyan employed; he was then changed to assistant administrator of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Juzheng was timid, silent, and incapable of managing affairs. Censorial officials led by Ouyang Xiu argued that Zhongyan had the makings of a chief minister and urged that Juzheng be dismissed in his favor. Zhongyan was then appointed Assistant Administrator of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 仲淹曰：「執政可由諫官而得乎？

translations.literal: Zhongyan said: "Can one obtain governing office through remonstrance officials?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan objected: "Is high office to be obtained through the push of censorial remonstrators?

sentences.zh: 」固辭不拜，願與韓琦出行邊。

translations.literal: He steadfastly declined and did not accept, wishing instead to go to the frontier with Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused the appointment and asked instead to serve on the frontier alongside Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 命為陝西宣撫使，未行，復除參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Shaanxi pacification commissioner; before he could depart, he was again appointed assistant administrator of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner, but before he could leave was again appointed Assistant Administrator of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會王倫寇淮南，州縣官有不能守者，朝廷欲按誅之。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Lun raided Huainan; among prefectural and county officials there were some who could not hold their posts, and the court wished to investigate and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun raided Huainan, some local officials had failed to hold their posts, and the court moved to prosecute and execute them.

sentences.zh: 仲淹曰：「平時諱言武備，寇至而專責守臣死事，可乎？

translations.literal: Zhongyan said: "In normal times military readiness is taboo to mention; when invaders arrive, to fix sole blame on defending officials to die in office—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan protested: "We forbid talk of military preparedness in peacetime, then when the enemy comes demand that local defenders die at their posts—is that right?

sentences.zh: 」守令皆得不誅。

translations.literal: The defending prefects and magistrates were all spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to him, none of the defending prefects and magistrates was put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝方銳意太平，數問當世事，仲淹語人曰：「上用我至矣，事有先後，久安之弊，非朝夕可革也。

translations.literal: The emperor was then keenly set on great peace and repeatedly asked about current affairs. Zhongyan told others: "The sovereign is using me to the full; affairs have an order of priority—the ills of long stability cannot be reformed overnight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was intensely devoted to lasting peace and often pressed Zhongyan on affairs of state. Zhongyan told colleagues: "The throne is relying on me completely—but reforms must come in order. The rot of long complacency cannot be scraped away in a day.

sentences.zh: 」帝再賜手詔，又為之開天章閣，召二府條對，仲淹皇恐，退而上十事：

translations.literal: The emperor twice bestowed handwritten edicts, and for him opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, summoning the two councils to respond item by item. Zhongyan, awed and fearful, withdrew and submitted ten proposals:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor twice sent personal edicts, opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations for him, and summoned the two councils to answer point by point. Overwhelmed, Zhongyan withdrew and submitted his ten reform items:

sentences.zh: 一曰明黜陟。

translations.literal: First: clarify promotions and demotions.
translations.idiomatic: First: make promotions and demotions transparent.

sentences.zh: 二府非有大功大善者不遷，內外須在職滿三年，在京百司非選舉而授，須通滿五年，乃得磨勘，庶幾考績之法矣。

translations.literal: Without great merit or great virtue, no one in the two councils should be transferred; inside and outside the capital one must serve a full three years; those in the hundred offices of the capital not appointed by examination must serve five years in total before review—then the method of assessing performance may be realized.
translations.idiomatic: No one in the two highest councils should be promoted without major merit. Officials inside and outside the capital must complete three full years in post; those in capital agencies appointed outside the examination system must serve five years before review. Only then can performance truly be measured.

sentences.zh: 二曰抑僥倖。

translations.literal: Second: restrain undeserved favor.
translations.idiomatic: Second: curb special privilege and undeserved favor.

sentences.zh: 罷少卿、監以上乾元節恩澤；

translations.literal: Abolish Qiankuan Festival favors for vice-ministers and commissioners and above;
translations.idiomatic: End the Qiankuan Festival perquisites granted to vice-ministers and supervisory commissioners and above;

sentences.zh: 正郎以下若監司、邊任，須在職滿二年，始得蔭子；

translations.literal: for rectifiers and below, as well as circuit intendants and frontier appointees, one must serve a full two years before gaining the privilege of extending office to one's sons;
translations.idiomatic: officials from rectifier rank downward, including circuit commissioners and frontier appointees, must serve two full years before their sons may inherit office;

sentences.zh: 大臣不得薦子弟任館閣職，蔭子之法無冗濫矣。

translations.literal: great ministers may not recommend their sons and younger brothers for archive and pavilion posts—then the method of extending office to sons will be free of excess and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: and senior ministers may not recommend their sons and nephews for prestigious archive posts. Then inheritance of office will no longer breed redundancy and abuse.

sentences.zh: 三曰精貢舉。

translations.literal: Third: refine the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Third: reform the civil-service examinations.

sentences.zh: 進士、諸科請罷糊名法，參考履行無闕者，以名聞。

translations.literal: For jinshi and the various examination categories, request abolishing the sealed-name method; for those whose conduct in office is without fault, report their names.
translations.idiomatic: For jinshi candidates and other degree tracks, abolish sealed-name grading; where conduct in office has been unblemished, report candidates by name.

sentences.zh: 進士先策論，後詩賦，諸科取兼通經義者。

translations.literal: For jinshi, policy essays first and then poetry and rhapsodies; for other categories, select those who broadly master the classics and their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Place policy essays before poetry and rhapsody for jinshi candidates; for other tracks, favor those with genuine mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 賜第以上，皆取詔裁。

translations.literal: For all granted ranks and above, leave appointment to imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: All honors at granted-rank level and above should require imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 餘優等免選注官，次第人守本科選。

translations.literal: The remaining excellent grades may skip selective appointment and receive direct posting; those below proceed according to the selection roster of their degree category.
translations.idiomatic: Top graduates may bypass further selection for appointment; others should advance strictly within their degree category.

sentences.zh: 進士之法，可以循名而責實矣。

translations.literal: Then the method for jinshi can match names to realities.
translations.idiomatic: Then the jinshi system can finally reward merit rather than empty credentials.

sentences.zh: 四曰擇長官。

translations.literal: Fourth: choose capable chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: appoint capable chief officials.

sentences.zh: 委中書、樞密院先選轉運使、提點刑獄、大藩知州；

translations.literal: Entrust the Secretariat and Privy Council first to select transport commissioners, judicial intendant commissioners, and prefects of major circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Let the Secretariat and Privy Council first choose transport commissioners, judicial intendants, and prefects of major circuits;

sentences.zh: 次委兩制、三司、御史台、開封府官、諸路監司舉知州、通判；

translations.literal: next entrust drafters of both grades, the three fiscal commissions, the Censorate, Kaifeng officials, and circuit commissioners to recommend prefects and vice-prefects;
translations.idiomatic: then assign drafters, fiscal commissioners, censorial officials, Kaifeng administrators, and circuit supervisors to recommend prefects and vice-prefects;

sentences.zh: 知州通判舉知縣、令。

translations.literal: prefects and vice-prefects recommend magistrates and district chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: and let prefects and vice-prefects nominate district magistrates and chiefs.

sentences.zh: 限其人數，以舉主多者從中書選除。

translations.literal: Limit the number of nominees; where recommending hosts are numerous, let the Secretariat choose and appoint from among them.
translations.idiomatic: Cap the number of nominees and have the Secretariat appoint from among those with the strongest backing.

sentences.zh: 刺史、縣令，可以得人矣。

translations.literal: Then prefectural and county chiefs can obtain the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Then prefects and magistrates can be chosen on merit.

sentences.zh: 五曰均公田。

translations.literal: Fifth: equalize official fields.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: equalize official salary lands.

sentences.zh: 外官廩給不均，何以求其為善耶？

translations.literal: When outer officials' grain stipends are unequal, how can one demand that they do good?
translations.idiomatic: When frontier officials receive unequal stipends, how can we expect them to govern honorably?

sentences.zh: 請均其入，第給之，使有以自養，然後可以責廉節，而不法者可誅廢矣。

translations.literal: Request equalizing their income and allotting it by rank, so they have means to support themselves; then one can hold them to integrity, and those who violate law may be punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Equalize their income and pay them properly so they can support themselves—then we can demand integrity, and punish or dismiss those who break the law.

sentences.zh: 六曰厚農桑。

translations.literal: Sixth: enrich agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: strengthen farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 每歲預下諸路，風吏民言農田利害，堤堰渠塘，州縣選官治之。

translations.literal: Each year send instructions down to the circuits in advance, encouraging officials and people to report the benefits and harms of farmland, dikes, weirs, canals, and ponds; let prefectures and counties select officials to manage them.
translations.idiomatic: Each year send orders to every circuit inviting officials and commoners to report on farmland, dikes, canals, and reservoirs; let local governments assign officials to manage improvements.

sentences.zh: 定勸課之法以興農利，減漕運。

translations.literal: Establish methods of encouragement and assessment to promote agricultural profit and reduce grain transport by canal.
translations.idiomatic: Set incentives to expand agricultural production and cut grain tribute shipments.

sentences.zh: 江南之圩田，浙西之河塘，隳廢者可興矣。

translations.literal: The polder fields of Jiangnan and the river embankments of western Zhejiang that lie ruined can be revived.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoned polders in Jiangnan and neglected river works in western Zhejiang can be restored.

sentences.zh: 七曰修武備。

translations.literal: Seventh: repair military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: rebuild military readiness.

sentences.zh: 約府兵法，募畿輔強壯為衛士，以助正兵。

translations.literal: Follow the garrison militia regulations, recruit strong men from the capital region as guard soldiers to assist the regular army.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt the garrison militia system and recruit able-bodied men from the capital region as local guards to supplement the regular army.

sentences.zh: 三時務農，一時教戰，省給贍之費。

translations.literal: Three seasons devoted to farming, one season to martial drill—saving the cost of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Let them farm three seasons and train one, cutting the cost of full-time pay.

sentences.zh: 畿輔有成法，則諸道皆可舉行矣。

translations.literal: Once the capital region has an established method, all circuits can likewise implement it.
translations.idiomatic: Establish the model in the capital region, then extend it to every circuit.

sentences.zh: 八曰推恩信。

translations.literal: Eighth: extend grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: enforce grace and keep the throne's word.

sentences.zh: 赦令有所施行，主司稽違者，重置於法；

translations.literal: When amnesty edicts are to be implemented, officials who delay or violate them should be heavily punished according to law;
translations.idiomatic: When amnesties are proclaimed, punish severely any official who stalls or obstructs them;

sentences.zh: 別遣使按視其所當行者，所在無廢格上恩者矣。

translations.literal: separately dispatch envoys to inspect what ought to be carried out—then nowhere will imperial grace be nullified.
translations.idiomatic: and send inspectors to ensure each order is carried out—so imperial mercy is never blocked on the ground.

sentences.zh: 九曰重命令。

translations.literal: Ninth: weight commands.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth: give laws lasting force.

sentences.zh: 法度所以示信也，行之未幾，旋即厘改。

translations.literal: Laws and standards exist to show trustworthiness, yet scarcely are they enforced before they are immediately revised.
translations.idiomatic: Laws exist to inspire trust, yet no sooner are they issued than they are changed again.

sentences.zh: 請政事之臣參議可以久行者，刪去煩冗，裁為制敕行下，命令不至於數變更矣。

translations.literal: Request that governing ministers jointly discuss what can long be carried out, delete what is redundant and burdensome, trim them into statutes and edicts for promulgation—then commands will not undergo repeated change.
translations.idiomatic: Have the chief ministers agree on durable reforms, cut redundancy, and issue them as binding statutes—so orders stop changing every month.

sentences.zh: 十曰減徭役。

translations.literal: Tenth: reduce corvée and labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth: reduce corvée burdens.

sentences.zh: 戶口耗少而供億滋多，省縣邑戶少者為鎮，並使、州兩院為一，職官白直，給以州兵，其不應受役者悉歸之農，民無重困之憂矣。

translations.literal: Households dwindle while supplies and transport multiply; reduce counties and districts with few households to market towns, merge the two bureaus of commissioner and prefect into one, assign official runners and guards, supply them with prefectural troops, and return all who should not bear corvée to farming—then the people will be free of the worry of crushing burdens.
translations.idiomatic: As population shrinks but levies grow, downgrade small counties to market towns, merge duplicate prefectural offices, assign runners and guards from prefectural troops, and release from corvée all who should be farming—then the people will be spared crushing burdens.

sentences.zh: 天子方信向仲淹，悉採用之，宜著令者，皆以詔書畫一頒下；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was then placing full trust in Zhongyan and adopted all of it; where regulations should be enacted, all were promulgated uniformly by edict;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Zhongyan completely and adopted nearly all of his program; measures fit to become law were issued in unified edicts;

sentences.zh: 獨府兵法，眾以為不可而止。

translations.literal: only the garrison militia regulations—the multitude thought them impracticable and they were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: only the garrison militia proposal was shelved after widespread objections.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「周制，三公分兼六官之職，漢以三公分部六卿，唐以宰相分判六曹。

translations.literal: He further submitted a proposal: "Under the Zhou system, the three dukes each also held the duties of the six ministries; in Han the three dukes divided supervision of the six ministers; in Tang the chief ministers each adjudicated one of the six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed: "Under Zhou, the three dukes shared the six ministries' duties; Han's three excellencies oversaw the six ministers; Tang's chief ministers each presided over one of the six bureaus.

sentences.zh: 今中書，古天官塚宰也，樞密院，古夏官司馬也。

translations.literal: Today the Secretariat is the ancient Director of Heaven, chief steward; the Privy Council is the ancient Minister of Summer, commander.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Secretariat corresponds to the ancient Grand Steward of Heaven; the Privy Council to the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四官散於群有司，無三公兼領之重。

translations.literal: The four offices are scattered among the many departments, without the weight of the three dukes holding concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their powers are scattered among a host of agencies, lacking the unified weight the three dukes once wielded.

sentences.zh: 而二府惟進擢差除，循資級，議賞罰，檢用條例而已。

translations.literal: Yet the two councils only advance, appoint, transfer, follow seniority, discuss rewards and punishments, and inspect and apply regulations—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The two councils today do little more than promote, appoint, track seniority, settle rewards and punishments, and apply regulations.

sentences.zh: 上非三公論道之任，下無六卿佐王之職，非治法也。

translations.literal: Above there is not the duty of the three dukes to discuss the Way; below there are not the six ministers assisting the king—this is not a method of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: At the top there is no grand counsel on statecraft; below there are no ministers truly assisting the throne. This is not sound governance.

sentences.zh: 臣請仿前代，以三司、司農、審官、流內銓、三班院、國子監、太常、刑部、審刑、大理、群牧、殿前馬步軍司，各委輔臣兼判其事。

translations.literal: Your servant requests following former ages: the Three Commissions, the Directorate of Agriculture, the Office of Personnel Review, the Internal Selection Office, the Three-Rank Court, the Directorate of Education, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Ministry of Justice, the Office of Judicial Review, the Court of Judicial Review, the Directorate of Herds, and the Bureau of Palace Cavalry and Infantry—each entrust an assisting minister concurrently to adjudicate its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we restore the old model: assign assisting ministers to concurrently oversee the Three Commissions, the agricultural directorate, personnel offices, the military roster bureaus, the imperial academy, the sacrificial court, the justice ministries, the herd directorate, and the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 凡官吏黜陟、刑法重輕、事有利害者，並從輔臣予奪：其體大者，二府僉議奏裁。

translations.literal: For all appointments and dismissals of officials, the weight of penal law, and matters of benefit or harm, let assisting ministers decide grant and denial; for those of large scope, let the two councils jointly discuss and submit for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Let assisting ministers decide promotions, dismissals, penalties, and any matter of real consequence; major questions should be jointly debated by the two councils and submitted for the throne's decision.

sentences.zh: 臣請自領兵賦之職，如其無補，請先黜降。

translations.literal: Your servant requests to personally take charge of military and fiscal duties; if they prove without benefit, ask first to be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: I offer to take personal charge of military and fiscal affairs myself—and if I fail, demote me first.

sentences.zh: 」章得象等皆曰不可。

translations.literal: Zhang Dexiang and others all said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dexiang and his allies objected that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃命參知政事賈昌朝領農田，仲淹領刑法，然卒不果行。

translations.literal: After a long while, Assistant Administrator Jia Changchao was finally ordered to oversee agricultural fields and Zhongyan to oversee penal law—yet in the end it was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Jia Changchao was assigned to oversee agriculture and Zhongyan criminal law—but in the end the plan never took effect.

sentences.zh: 初，仲淹以忤呂夷簡，放逐者數年，士大夫持二人曲直，交指為朋黨。

translations.literal: At first, because Zhongyan had offended Lü Yijian, he was exiled for several years; scholar-officials took sides on the rights and wrongs of the two men and in turn denounced them as faction members.
translations.idiomatic: Years earlier Zhongyan had crossed Lü Yijian and was banished for several years. Officials took sides in their feud and began calling each camp a clique.

sentences.zh: 及陝西用兵，天子以仲淹士望所屬，拔用之。

translations.literal: When military operations began in Shaanxi, the Son of Heaven, because scholar-officials' esteem rested on Zhongyan, pulled him out and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Shaanxi, the emperor raised Zhongyan because the scholarly elite looked to him.

sentences.zh: 及夷簡罷，召還，倚以為治，中外想望其功業。

translations.literal: When Yijian was dismissed, Zhongyan was recalled; the throne relied on him for governance, and inside and outside the court looked to his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: After Yijian fell from power, Zhongyan was recalled and entrusted with reform. Court and country alike looked to him for great deeds.

sentences.zh: 而仲淹以天下為己任，裁削幸濫，考覈官吏，日夜謀慮興致太平。

translations.literal: Yet Zhongyan took the realm as his own charge, trimmed favoritism and excess, examined officials, and day and night plotted how to bring about great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan took the empire as his personal charge—cutting favoritism, auditing officials, and working day and night toward lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 然更張無漸，規摹闊大，論者以為不可行。

translations.literal: Yet his reforms had no gradual pace; their scope was vast, and critics held them impracticable.
translations.idiomatic: But he moved too fast and planned too broadly; critics called his program unworkable.

sentences.zh: 及按察使出，多所舉劾，人心不悅。

translations.literal: When investigative commissioners went out, they impeached many; popular sentiment was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When his investigative commissioners went out and impeached officials far and wide, resentment spread.

sentences.zh: 自任子之恩薄，磨勘之法密，僥倖者不便，於是謗毀稍行，而朋黨之論浸聞上矣。

translations.literal: From the thinning of sons' inheritance privilege and the tightening of review methods, those who relied on undeserved fortune were discommoded; then slander gradually spread, and talk of factions gradually reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: As inherited office grew harder to obtain and performance reviews tightened, those who lived on privilege grew restless. Slander spread, and whispers of factionalism gradually reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會邊陲有警，因與樞密副使富弼請行邊。

translations.literal: It happened that the frontier was alarmed; accordingly he and Vice Commissioner Fu Bi requested to go to the border.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble flared on the frontier, he and Vice Commissioner Fu Bi asked to go oversee the borders.

sentences.zh: 於是，以仲淹為河東、陝西宣撫使，賜黃金百兩，悉分遺邊將。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongyan was made pacification commissioner of Hedong and Shaanxi; he was granted a hundred taels of gold, all of which he distributed to frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Hedong and Shaanxi, granted a hundred taels of gold, and gave every ounce to frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 麟州新罹大寇，言者多請棄之，仲淹為修故砦，招還流亡三千餘戶，蠲其稅，罷榷酤予民。

translations.literal: Lin Prefecture had recently suffered a great raid; many urged abandoning it. Zhongyan restored old forts, summoned back more than three thousand refugee households, remitted their taxes, and abolished the liquor monopoly to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Prefecture had just been ravaged; many urged abandoning it. Zhongyan rebuilt old forts, brought back more than three thousand refugee families, waived their taxes, and lifted the liquor monopoly for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 又奏免府州商稅，河外遂安。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to exempt commercial taxes at Fu Prefecture, and the region west of the Yellow River was then secure.
translations.idiomatic: He also secured exemption of commercial taxes at Fu Prefecture, and the country west of the river was finally at peace.

sentences.zh: 比去。

translations.literal: When he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took his leave.

sentences.zh: 攻者益急，仲淹亦自請罷政事，乃以為資政殿學士、陝西四路宣撫使、知邠州。

translations.literal: Those who attacked grew more urgent; Zhongyan also requested on his own to resign from state affairs, and he was then made Academician of the Zizheng Hall, Pacification Commissioner of the four circuits of Shaanxi, and Prefect of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His attackers pressed harder still, and Zhongyan himself asked to leave the council. He was then made Academician of the Zizheng Hall, Pacification Commissioner for the four Shaanxi circuits, and Prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 其在中書所施為，亦稍稍沮罷。

translations.literal: What he had carried out in the Secretariat was also gradually obstructed and halted.
translations.idiomatic: The reforms he had begun in the Secretariat were gradually undone.

sentences.zh: 以疾請鄧州，進給事中。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested Deng Prefecture, and was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he asked to be sent to Deng Prefecture and was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 徙荊南，鄧人遮使者請留，仲淹亦願留鄧，許之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jingnan; the people of Deng blocked the messenger and asked that he stay; Zhongyan also wished to remain at Deng, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he was reassigned to Jingnan, the people of Deng waylaid the imperial messenger and begged to keep him. Zhongyan wanted to stay as well, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋徙杭州，再遷戶部侍郎，徙青州。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Hang Prefecture, then again promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and transferred to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Hangzhou, promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and then transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會病甚，請潁州，未至而卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: It happened that his illness was severe; he requested Ying Prefecture, but before arriving he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened. He asked to go to Yingzhou but died before he arrived, at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書，諡文正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of War, with the posthumous title Wen Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Minister of War and gave him the posthumous name Wen Zheng, "Upright in Culture."

sentences.zh: 初，仲淹病，帝常遣使賜藥存問，既卒，嗟悼久之。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhongyan was ill, the emperor often sent envoys to grant medicine and inquire after him; when he had died, the emperor sighed in mourning for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: During his illness the emperor often sent medicine and inquiries. When he died, the emperor mourned him at length.

sentences.zh: 又遣使就問其家，既葬，帝親書其碑曰「褒賢之碑。」

translations.literal: The emperor again sent an envoy to visit his family; after the burial, the emperor personally wrote his stele: "Stele in Praise of Worth."
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy to condole with the family, and after the funeral personally inscribed the memorial stele: "Monument to a Worthy Man."

sentences.zh: 仲淹內剛外和，性至孝，以母在時方貧，其後雖貴，非賓客不重肉。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was firm within and harmonious without; his nature was utterly filial. Because his mother had lived in poverty, even after he grew eminent he did not serve a second meat dish except to guests.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was steely within and gentle without, and deeply filial. Having known poverty while his mother lived, he remained sparing even in high office, serving meat only to guests.

sentences.zh: 妻子衣食，僅能自充。

translations.literal: His wife and children's food and clothing barely sufficed for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His family's food and clothing were scarcely more than bare necessity.

sentences.zh: 而好施予，置義莊里中，以贍族人。

translations.literal: Yet he loved to give; he established a charitable estate in the village to support clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved to give generously, founding a charitable estate in his home village to support kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 泛愛樂善，士多出其門下，雖里巷之人，皆能道其名字。

translations.literal: His universal love and delight in goodness were such that many scholars came from under his gate; even people in lanes and alleys could speak his name.
translations.idiomatic: He loved widely and delighted in good deeds. Many scholars passed through his tutelage, and even common folk in the lanes knew his name.

sentences.zh: 死之日，四方聞者，皆為歎息。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, all who heard from the four quarters sighed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, people far and wide sighed in grief.

sentences.zh: 為政尚忠厚，所至有恩，邠、慶二州之民與屬羌，皆畫像立生祠事之。

translations.literal: In governing he honored loyalty and kindness; wherever he went there was grace. The people of Bin and Qing prefectures and the dependent Qiang all painted his likeness and raised living shrines to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he prized loyalty and kindness and left grace wherever he served. In Bin and Qing, Chinese subjects and dependent Qiang alike painted his portrait and raised living shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 及其卒也，羌酋數百人，哭之如父，齋三日而去。

translations.literal: When he died, several hundred Qiang chieftains wept for him as for a father, fasted three days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, hundreds of Qiang chieftains mourned him as they would a father, kept three days of abstinence, and then departed.

sentences.zh: 四子：純祐、純仁、純禮、純粹。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Chunyou, Chunren, Chun Li, and Chun Cui.
