translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Chunyou, Chunren, Chun Li, and Chun Cui.

sentences.zh: 子 純祐

translations.literal: Son: Chunyou
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunyou

sentences.zh: 純祐，字天成，性英悟自得，尚節行。

translations.literal: Chunyou, styled Tiancheng, was by nature brilliantly perceptive and self-possessed, and honored integrity in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou, styled Tiancheng, was brilliantly perceptive and self-possessed, and prized moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 方十歲，能讀諸書；

translations.literal: At just ten years, he could read all the classics;
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could read the full canon;

sentences.zh: 為文章，籍籍有稱。

translations.literal: in composing essays he won widespread renown.
translations.idiomatic: and his essays already won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 父仲淹守蘇州，首建郡學，聘胡瑗為師。

translations.literal: When his father Zhongyan was prefect of Suzhou, he first established the prefectural school and engaged Hu Yuan as master.
translations.idiomatic: When his father served as prefect of Suzhou, he founded the prefectural school and engaged Hu Yuan as its master.

sentences.zh: 瑗立學規良密，生徒數百，多不率教，仲淹患之。

translations.literal: Hu Yuan established school regulations of fine strictness; student disciples numbered in the hundreds, and many did not follow instruction—Zhongyan was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuan laid down exacting rules, but among hundreds of students many would not obey. Zhongyan was troubled.

sentences.zh: 純祐尚未冠，輒白入學，齒諸生之末，盡行其規，諸生隨之，遂不敢犯。

translations.literal: Chunyou had not yet come of age, yet declared himself entered into study, took his place at the end of the students, fully carried out the regulations, and the students followed—then none dared transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou, not yet of age, enrolled himself, stood at the end of the student ranks, and followed every rule to the letter. The others followed, and violations ceased.

sentences.zh: 自是蘇學為諸郡倡。

translations.literal: From this the Suzhou school became the model for all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Suzhou's school became the model for every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寶元中，西夏叛，仲淹連官關陝，皆將兵。

translations.literal: In the Baoyuan era the Western Xia rebelled; Zhongyan held successive posts in the Guan-Shaan region, all commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoyuan reign the Western Xia rebelled. Zhongyan held successive posts along the Guan-Shaan frontier, each time in command of troops.

sentences.zh: 純祐與將卒錯處，鉤深擿隱，得其才否。

translations.literal: Chunyou mixed with generals and soldiers, probing deeply and drawing out what was hidden, learning who had talent and who did not.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou lived among officers and soldiers, probing deeply and learning who had real talent and who did not.

sentences.zh: 由是仲淹任人無失，而屢有功。

translations.literal: By this Zhongyan made appointments without error and repeatedly won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhongyan chose men without error and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 仲淹帥環慶，議城馬鋪砦，砦逼夏境，夏懼扼其沖，侵撓其役。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan commanded Huan and Qing, he proposed building a fort at Mapu Stockade; the stockade pressed the Xia border, and Xia feared throttling of their vital route and harassed the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyan commanded Huanqing circuit, he proposed fortifying Mapu Stockade on the Xia border. The Xia, fearing stranglehold of a vital route, harassed the construction crews.

sentences.zh: 純祐率兵馳據其地，夏眾大至，且戰且役，數日而成，一路恃之以安。

translations.literal: Chunyou led troops in a rush to seize the ground; a great Xia force arrived, and they fought even as they worked; in several days it was finished, and the whole circuit relied on it for security.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou rushed troops to hold the site. A large Xia force arrived, but they fought while they built, and in days the fort was done. The whole circuit found security in it.

sentences.zh: 純祐事父母孝，未嘗違左右，不應科第。

translations.literal: Chunyou served his parents filially, never leaving their side, and did not take the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Filial toward his parents, he never left their side and refused the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 及仲淹以讒罷，純祐不得已，蔭守將作監主簿，又為司竹監，以非所好，即解去。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan was dismissed through slander, Chunyou had no choice but to inherit appointment as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Construction, then served as Superintendent of Bamboo Plantations; because these were not to his liking, he immediately resigned.
translations.idiomatic: When slander brought Zhongyan down, Chunyou reluctantly accepted inherited appointment as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Construction, then Superintendent of Bamboo Plantations. Finding neither post to his taste, he resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 從仲淹之鄧，得疾昏廢，臥許昌。

translations.literal: He followed Zhongyan to Deng, fell ill to the point of collapse, and lay bedridden at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhongyan to Deng, fell gravely ill, and took to his bed at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 富弼守淮西，過省之，猶能感慨道忠義，問弼之來公耶私耶，弼曰「公」。

translations.literal: Fu Bi, guarding the Huai west, passed by to visit him; Chunyou could still speak feelingly of loyalty and righteousness, and asked whether Bi's visit was public or private; Bi said, "Public."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi, posted to the Huai west, stopped to visit him. Even bedridden, Chunyou could still speak passionately of loyalty and duty. He asked whether Fu had come on public business or private; Fu answered, "Public."

sentences.zh: 純祐曰「公則可」。

translations.literal: Chunyou said, "If public, then it is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou said, "Then it is acceptable."

sentences.zh: 凡病十九年卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In all he was ill nineteen years before he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was ill for nineteen years before he died, at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子正臣，守太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: His son was Zheng Chen, who served as libationer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng Chen served as libationer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 子 純禮

translations.literal: Son: Chun Li
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun Li

sentences.zh: 純禮，字彝叟，以父仲淹蔭，為秘書省正字，簽書河南府判官，知陵台令兼永安縣。

translations.literal: Chun Li, styled Yisou, by his father Zhongyan's privilege became corrector of the Secretariat, signed as administrative assistant of Henan Prefecture, and served as magistrate of Lingtai and concurrently of Yong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li, styled Yisou, entered office through his father's privilege as corrector in the Secretariat, deputy administrator of Henan Prefecture, and magistrate of Lingtai while concurrently overseeing Yong'an County.

sentences.zh: 永昭陵建，京西轉運使配木石磚甓及工徒於一路，獨永安不受令。

translations.literal: When Yongzhao Mausoleum was built, the transport commissioner of Jingxi apportioned timber, stone, bricks, tiles, and labor across the circuit; Yong'an alone refused the order.
translations.idiomatic: During construction of Yongzhao Mausoleum, the Jingxi transport commissioner apportioned timber, stone, brick, tile, and labor across the circuit. Yong'an alone refused.

sentences.zh: 使者以白陵使韓琦，琦曰：「范純禮豈不知此？

translations.literal: The envoy reported this to the mausoleum commissioner Han Qi, who said: "Would Fan Chun Li not know this?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported to mausoleum commissioner Han Qi, who said, "Fan Chun Li must know what he is doing—

sentences.zh: 將必有說。

translations.literal: Surely he must have a reason.
translations.idiomatic: he must have his reasons.

sentences.zh: 」他日，眾質之，純禮曰：「陵寢皆在邑境，歲時繕治無虛日，今乃與百縣均賦，曷若置此，使之奉常時用乎。

translations.literal: " On another day the crowd questioned him; Chun Li said: "The tombs all lie within the county's territory; year-round maintenance has no idle day. Now to levy equally with a hundred counties—how does that compare with setting this aside so it may supply routine needs?
translations.idiomatic: " Later, when others questioned him, Chun Li said, "The imperial tombs all lie within my county, and year-round upkeep keeps us busy every day. Why levy us equally with a hundred other counties? Better reserve these resources for ordinary maintenance."

sentences.zh: 」琦是其對。

translations.literal: " Qi approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi approved.

sentences.zh: 還朝，用為三司鹽鐵判官，以比部員外郎出知遂州。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was appointed salt and iron judge of the Three Commissions, and left office as outer adjunct of the Ministry of Revenue to serve as prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he became salt and iron judge of the Three Commissions, then left as outer adjunct of the Ministry of Revenue to govern Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 滬南有邊事，調度苛棘，純禮一以靜待之，辨其可具者，不取於民。

translations.literal: South of the Hu there were frontier affairs; levies were harsh and difficult. Chun Li met all with calm, distinguishing what could be supplied without taking from the people.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier troubles south of the Hu brought harsh levies, Chun Li met them with calm, supplying only what could be furnished without taxing the people.

sentences.zh: 民圖像於廬，而奉之如神，名曰「范公庵」。

translations.literal: The people painted his likeness in a hut and venerated him as a spirit, calling it "Hermitage of Lord Fan."
translations.idiomatic: The people painted his portrait in a roadside shrine and worshipped him like a god, naming it the Hermitage of Lord Fan.

sentences.zh: 草場火，民情疑怖，守吏惕息俟誅。

translations.literal: A hay depot caught fire; popular sentiment was fearful and suspicious; the guarding officials trembled and awaited execution.
translations.idiomatic: When a hay depot burned, the people were frightened and suspicious, and the responsible officials trembled, awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 純禮曰：「草濕則生火，何足怪！

translations.literal: Chun Li said: "When grass is damp it can catch fire—what is there to marvel at!
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li said, "Damp hay catches fire—what is strange in that?

sentences.zh: 」但使密償之。

translations.literal: " He simply had it quietly compensated.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the loss quietly reimbursed.

sentences.zh: 庫吏盜絲多罪至死，純禮曰：「以棼然之絲而殺之，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: Warehouse clerks who stole much silk were liable to death; Chun Li said: "To kill a man over tangled silk—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Warehouse clerks who stole silk faced death. Chun Li said, "I cannot bear to kill a man over a tangle of thread.

sentences.zh: 」聽其家趣買以贖，命釋其株連者。

translations.literal: " He allowed their families to hurry to purchase ransom, and ordered release of those implicated with them.
translations.idiomatic: " He let their families pay restitution to redeem them and ordered the release of those implicated.

sentences.zh: 除戶部郎中、京西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of the Ministry of Revenue and deputy transport commissioner of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Ministry of Revenue and deputy Jingxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，入為吏部郎中，遷左司。

translations.literal: At the start of the Yuanyou era he entered service as director of the Ministry of Personnel and was transferred to the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he entered the capital as director of the Ministry of Personnel, then moved to the Left Office.

sentences.zh: 又遷太常少卿、江淮荊浙發運使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commissioner of Grain Transport for the Jiang-Huai, Jing, and Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commissioner of Grain Transport for the Jiang-Huai, Jing, and Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 以光祿卿召，遷刑部侍郎，進給事中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Chamberlain for Imperial Ceremonial, transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, and promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Chamberlain for Imperial Ceremonial, he became Vice Minister of Justice and then Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 純禮凡所封駁，正名分紀綱，皆國體之大者。

translations.literal: In all the memorials Chun Li drafted or rejected, he set right names and discipline—matters great to the body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In every memorial he drafted or rejected, Chun Li upheld proper titles and institutional order—matters that touched the nation's core.

sentences.zh: 張耒除起居舍人，病未能朝，而令先供職。

translations.literal: Zhang Lei was appointed Attendant Herald, was ill and unable to attend court, yet was ordered to take up duty first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lei was appointed Attendant Herald but, though too ill for court, was ordered to assume office first.

sentences.zh: 純禮批敕曰：「臣僚未有以疾謁告，不赴朝參先視事者。

translations.literal: Chun Li annotated the edict: "There has never been a case of a ministerial official taking leave for illness, failing to attend court audience, yet handling affairs first.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li annotated the draft edict: "No official has ever taken sick leave, skipped court audience, and begun work anyway.

sentences.zh: 耒能供職，豈不能見君？

translations.literal: If Lei can perform his duties, can he not see the sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: If Lei is well enough to serve, is he not well enough to see the emperor?

sentences.zh: 壞禮亂法，所不當為。

translations.literal: To ruin ritual and disorder law—this ought not be done.
translations.idiomatic: That would wreck ritual and law, and must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 」聞者皆悚動。

translations.literal: " All who heard were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it were shaken.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞擊執政，將遂代其位，先以諷純禮。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief attacked the chief administrators and was about to succeed to their position; he first tried to sound out Chun Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief attacked the chief ministers and was poised to replace them. He first sounded out Chun Li.

sentences.zh: 純禮曰：「論人而奪之位，寧不避嫌邪？

translations.literal: Chun Li said: "To discuss a man and then seize his post—should one not avoid suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li said, "You criticize a man and then take his post—should you not at least avoid the appearance of it?

sentences.zh: 命果下，吾必還之。

translations.literal: If the appointment truly comes down, I shall certainly return it.
translations.idiomatic: If the appointment issues, I will certainly return the seal.

sentences.zh: 」宰相即徙純禮刑部侍郎，而後出命。

translations.literal: " The chief minister thereupon transferred Chun Li to Vice Minister of Justice, and only then issued the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister transferred Chun Li to Vice Minister of Justice first, then issued the appointment.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部，改天章閣待制、樞密都承旨，去知亳州、提舉明道宮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, changed to Pavilion Attendant of the Tianzhang Hall and Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then left to govern Bozhou and supervise the Mingdao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Personnel, became Pavilion Attendant of the Tianzhang Hall and Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then left to govern Bozhou and oversee Mingdao Palace.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，以龍圖閣直學士知開封府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, he was made Straight Academician of the Longtu Hall and Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne, Chun Li became Straight Academician of the Longtu Hall and Prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 前尹以刻深為治，純禮曰：「寬猛相濟，聖人之訓。

translations.literal: The previous prefect had governed through harsh severity; Chun Li said: "Leniency and severity complement each other—such is the sage's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect had ruled with harsh severity. Chun Li said, "Leniency and severity must balance each other—that is the sage's teaching.

sentences.zh: 今處深文之後，若益以猛，是以火濟火也。

translations.literal: Now, coming after deep severity in law, if one adds further harshness, that is using fire to remedy fire.
translations.idiomatic: After such deep severity in law, piling on more harshness is fighting fire with fire.

sentences.zh: 方務去前之苛，猶慮未盡，豈有寬為患也。

translations.literal: We are just trying to remove the previous harshness and still fear it is not enough—how could leniency become a harm?
translations.idiomatic: We are only beginning to undo past harshness and still fear we have not gone far enough—how could leniency itself be the danger?

sentences.zh: 」由是一切以寬處之。

translations.literal: " From this he handled everything with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he handled every matter with leniency.

sentences.zh: 中旨鞫享澤村民謀逆，純禮審其故，此民入戲場觀優，歸途見匠者作桶，取而戴於首曰：「與劉先生如何？

translations.literal: An imperial directive ordered investigation of Xiangze villagers for plotting rebellion; Chun Li examined the matter: this man entered a playhouse to watch performers, and on the way home saw a craftsman making a bucket, took it and put it on his head, saying: "How does this compare with Master Liu?
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order came to try Xiangze villagers for treason. Chun Li investigated and found that one man had gone to a playhouse, and on the way home saw a craftsman making a bucket, put it on his head, and said, "How does this compare with Master Liu?"

sentences.zh: 」遂為匠擒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the craftsman seized him.
translations.idiomatic: The craftsman seized him.

sentences.zh: 明日入對，徽宗問何以處之，對曰：「愚人村野無所知，若以叛逆蔽罪，恐辜好生之德，以不應為杖之，足矣。

translations.literal: The next day he entered audience; Huizong asked how to deal with it; he replied: "A foolish man of the countryside knew nothing; if one covered the crime as rebellion, one might fail the virtue of cherishing life—to punish him with the rod for doing what he ought not suffices.
translations.idiomatic: The next day at audience Huizong asked how to punish the man. Chun Li replied, "He was a foolish villager who knew nothing. To call that treason would betray the virtue of sparing life. A beating for improper conduct is enough."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「何以戒後人？

translations.literal: " [Huizong] said: "How then to warn posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Huizong asked, "How will that warn others?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「正欲外間知陛下刑憲不濫，足以為訓爾。

translations.literal: " He said: "It is precisely so the outside world may know that Your Majesty's punishments and laws are not excessive—enough to serve as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li answered, "Precisely so people will know Your Majesty's punishments are not excessive—that itself is the lesson."

sentences.zh: 」徽宗從之。

translations.literal: " Huizong assented.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部尚書，擢尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Rites and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 侍御史陳次升乞除罷言官並自內批，不由三省進擬，右相曾布力爭不能得，乞降黜次升。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Chen Cisheng requested dismissal of censorial officials by inner draft, not through the Three Departments for nomination; the Right Chancellor Zeng Bu argued fiercely but could not prevail, and requested Chen Cisheng's demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Chen Cisheng asked that censorial officials be dismissed by inner palace draft, bypassing the Three Departments. Right Chancellor Zeng Bu fought the proposal in vain and asked that Chen be demoted.

sentences.zh: 純禮徐進曰：「次升何罪？

translations.literal: Chun Li advanced slowly and said: "What crime has Cisheng committed?
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li said calmly, "What crime has Chen Cisheng committed?"

sentences.zh: 不過防柄臣各引所親，且去不附己者爾。

translations.literal: Nothing beyond guarding against powerful ministers each advancing their favorites and removing those who do not attach to themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing more than guarding against powerful ministers advancing their own men and clearing out those who will not serve them.

sentences.zh: 」徽宗曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Huizong said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong said, "True."

sentences.zh: 」乃寢布議。

translations.literal: " The proposal of Bu was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu's proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿告老，徽宗問執政，執政欲許之。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing asked to retire on grounds of age; Huizong questioned the chief administrators, who wished to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Huiqing asked to retire, Huizong consulted the chief ministers, who wanted to grant it.

sentences.zh: 純禮曰：「惠卿嘗輔政，其人固不足重，然當存國體。

translations.literal: Chun Li said: "Huiqing once assisted in government; the man is indeed not worth esteem, yet the dignity of the state ought be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li said, "Huiqing once served in government. The man may not deserve honor, but the dignity of the state must be preserved."

sentences.zh: 」曾布奏：「議者多憂財用不足，此非所急也，願陛下勿以為慮。

translations.literal: " Zeng Bu memorialized: "Many in deliberation worry that revenues are insufficient; this is not what is urgent—Your Majesty, please do not take it as a concern.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu memorialized, "Many worry about revenue shortfalls, but that is not urgent. Your Majesty need not concern yourself."

sentences.zh: 」純禮曰：「古者無三年之蓄，曰國非其國。

translations.literal: " Chun Li said: "In antiquity, lacking stores for three years was called making the state no state.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Li replied, "In antiquity they said that without three years' reserves, the state is no state at all."

sentences.zh: 今大農告匱，帑庾枵空，而曰不足慮，非面謾邪？

translations.literal: Now the chief granary reports shortage; treasuries and storehouses are hollow—and to say it is no concern, is that not deceiving to one's face?
translations.idiomatic: The chief granary reports shortfall and the treasuries are empty. To call that no concern—is that not bare-faced deceit?

sentences.zh: 」因從容諫曰：「邇者朝廷命令，莫不是元豐而非元祐。

translations.literal: " He then, at ease, remonstrated: "Of late court orders have all affirmed the Yuansfeng and rejected the Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: Then, in measured remonstrance, he said, "Recent court orders affirm Yuansfeng and reject Yuanyou at every turn."

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，神宗立法之意固善，吏推行之，或有失當，以致病民。

translations.literal: In my view, the intent of Emperor Shenzong's legislation was fundamentally good; when clerks carried it out, there were sometimes improprieties that harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: In my view Shenzong's legislative intent was fundamentally sound, but when officials enforced it they sometimes went wrong and harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 宣仁聽斷，一時小有潤色，蓋大臣識見異同，非必盡懷邪為私也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren's governance brought slight polish for a time; it was simply that great ministers' views differed—not that all necessarily harbored wicked private aims.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Xuanren there were modest improvements for a time. Great ministers simply differed in outlook—not all were driven by wicked private aims.

sentences.zh: 今議論之臣，有不得志，故挾此藉口。

translations.literal: Now among officials in debate, some are frustrated in ambition, and so seize on this as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Today some disputants, frustrated in ambition, seize on this as a pretext.

sentences.zh: 以元豐為是，則欲賢元豐之人；

translations.literal: To hold Yuansfeng right is to wish to honor Yuansfeng men;
translations.idiomatic: To praise Yuansfeng is to promote Yuansfeng men;

sentences.zh: 以元祐為非，則欲斥元祐之士，其心豈恤國事？

translations.literal: to hold Yuanyou wrong is to wish to expel Yuanyou scholars—do their hearts truly care for state affairs?
translations.idiomatic: to condemn Yuanyou is to purge Yuanyou men. Do their hearts truly care for the state?

sentences.zh: 直欲快私忿以售其奸，不可不深察也。」

translations.literal: They simply wish to satisfy private resentment and accomplish their treachery—this cannot but be examined deeply."
translations.idiomatic: They only want private vengeance and a path to intrigue. Your Majesty must look deeply into this."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「自古天下汨亂，系於用人。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since antiquity the flooding chaos of the realm has hinged on the appointment of men.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Since antiquity the ruin of realms has always hinged on whom rulers employ."

sentences.zh: 祖宗於此，最得其要。

translations.literal: Our ancestors in this grasped the essential point best.
translations.idiomatic: Our founders understood this better than anyone.

sentences.zh: 太祖用呂餘慶，太宗用王禹偁，真宗用張知白，皆從下列置諸要途。

translations.literal: Taizu employed Lü Yuqing, Taizong employed Wang Yucheng, Zhenzong employed Zhang Zhibai—all were placed on vital paths from lower ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu elevated Lü Yuqing, Taizong Wang Yucheng, and Zhenzong Zhang Zhibai—all men promoted from the lower ranks to critical posts.

sentences.zh: 人君欲得英傑之心，固當不次飭拔。

translations.literal: If a ruler wishes to win the hearts of outstanding men, he ought by all means to promote them out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler means to win the loyalty of outstanding men, he must promote them out of turn.

sentences.zh: 必待薦而後用，則守正特立之士，將終身晦跡矣。

translations.literal: If one must wait for recommendation before employing them, then upright and independent gentlemen will hide their traces all their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Men who wait only for recommendation before appointment will never see upright, independent talent emerge from obscurity.

sentences.zh: 」左司諫江公望論繼述事當執中道，不可拘一偏。

translations.literal: " Left Remonstrance Chief Jiang Gongwang argued that on matters of succession one should hold the middle way and not be bound to one extreme.
translations.idiomatic: " Left Remonstrance Chief Jiang Gongwang argued that on questions of inheriting the prior reign one should take the balanced course, not cling to one extreme.

sentences.zh: 徽宗出示其疏，純禮贊之曰：「願陛下以曉中外，使知聖意所向，亦足以革小人徇利之情。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong displayed his memorial; Chun Li praised it, saying: "Your Majesty, I beg that you make this clear within and without, so all may know where the sacred mind is tending—it would also suffice to reform the sentiment of petty men who pursue profit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong showed the memorial, Chun Li praised it: "Your Majesty should make this known at court and across the realm, so that all may see where you intend to lead—and petty men bent on private gain may be changed as well.

sentences.zh: 乞褒遷公望，以勸來者。」

translations.literal: I beg that Gongwang be rewarded and promoted, to encourage those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Gongwang be honored and promoted, to encourage others who follow."

sentences.zh: 純禮沉毅剛正，曾布憚之，激駙馬都尉王詵曰：「上欲除君承旨，范右丞不可。

translations.literal: Chun Li was deep, resolute, and upright; Zeng Bu feared him and goaded Imperial Son-in-Law Wang Shen, saying: "The emperor wishes to appoint you Hanlin Academic Expositor; Fan the Right Vice Chancellor will not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply reserved, resolute, and upright, Chun Li was feared by Zeng Bu, who stirred up Imperial Son-in-Law Wang Shen: "The emperor means to make you Hanlin academic expositor—but Fan the Right Vice Chancellor will block it.

sentences.zh: 」詵怒。

translations.literal: " Shen was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 會詵館遼使，純禮主宴，詵誣其輒斥御名，罷為端明殿學士、知潁昌府，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: When Shen was hosting Liao envoys, Chun Li presided over the banquet; Shen falsely accused him of rashly uttering the imperial taboo name. Chun Li was dismissed to be academician of the Hall of Brilliant Patterns, prefect of Yingchang, and administrator of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen was hosting envoys from Liao, Chun Li presided at the banquet. Shen falsely accused him of using the emperor's taboo name. Chun Li was removed to academician of the Hall of Brilliant Patterns, made prefect of Yingchang, and assigned to administer Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，啟黨禁，貶試少府監，分司南京。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era the faction ban was revived; he was demoted to probationary director of the Palace Storehouses with duty at the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongning, when the faction ban was revived, he was demoted to probationary director of the Palace Storehouses and assigned to the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 又貶靜江軍節度副使，徐州安置，徙單州。

translations.literal: He was further demoted to vice military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, placed under restraint at Xuzhou, and transferred to Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to vice military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, confined at Xuzhou, and later transferred to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，復左朝議大夫，提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was restored to Left Remonstrance Grand Master and made administrator of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he was restored as Left Remonstrance Grand Master and administrator of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 子 純粹

translations.literal: Son: Chun Cui
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun Cui

sentences.zh: 純粹，字德孺，以蔭遷至贊善大夫、檢正中書刑房，與同列有爭，出知滕縣，遷提舉成都諸路茶場。

translations.literal: Chun Cui, styled Deru, by privilege rose to Grand Master for Governance and rectifier of the Criminal Section in the Secretariat Chancellery; after a dispute with colleagues he was sent out as magistrate of Teng County, then promoted to administrator of the tea market of the several Chengdu circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Cui, styled Deru, rose through his father's privilege to Grand Master for Governance and rectifier of the Criminal Section in the Secretariat. After a dispute with colleagues he was posted as magistrate of Teng County, then put in charge of the tea market across the Chengdu circuits.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，為陝西轉運判官。

translations.literal: In the Yuansfeng era he served as transport vice commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuansfeng he served as Shaanxi transport vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時五路出師伐西夏：高遵裕出環慶，劉昌祚出涇原，李憲出熙河，种諤出鄜延，王中正出河東。

translations.literal: At the time five routes marched out to attack Western Xia: Gao Zunyu from Huanqing, Liu Changzuo from Jingyuan, Li Xian from Xihe, Zhong E from Yanyan, and Wang Zhongzheng from Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Five armies were then dispatched against Western Xia: Gao Zunyu from Huanqing, Liu Changzuo from Jingyuan, Li Xian from Xihe, Zhong E from Yanyan, and Wang Zhongzheng from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遵裕怒昌祚後期，欲按誅之，昌祚憂恚病臥，其麾下皆憤焉。

translations.literal: Zunyu was angry that Changzuo was late and wished to prosecute and execute him; Changzuo, aggrieved and resentful, fell ill and took to bed, and his subordinates were all furious.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyu was furious that Changzuo had arrived late and sought to have him prosecuted and executed. Changzuo, sick with grief and rage, took to his bed, and his troops seethed with indignation.

sentences.zh: 純粹恐兩軍不協，致生他變，勸遵裕往問昌祚疾，其難遂解。

translations.literal: Chun Cui feared the two armies would not cooperate and might produce other trouble; he urged Zunyu to go inquire after Changzuo's illness, and the difficulty was thus resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Cui feared discord between the two armies might spark further trouble and urged Zunyu to visit Changzuo's sickbed. The crisis was resolved.

sentences.zh: 神宗責諸將無功，謀欲再舉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong reproached the generals for achieving nothing and planned to campaign again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong blamed the generals for their failure and planned another campaign.

sentences.zh: 純粹奏：「關陝事力單竭，公私大困，若復加騷動，根本可憂。

translations.literal: Chun Cui memorialized: "The strength of Guan and Shaan is already exhausted; public and private affairs are greatly distressed. If we add further disturbance, the foundations will be cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Cui memorialized: "Guan and Shaan are spent; public finances and private households alike are in distress. Another upheaval would endanger the foundations of the realm.

sentences.zh: 異時言者必職臣是咎，臣寧受盡言之罪於今日，不忍默默以貽後悔。

translations.literal: When the time comes critics will surely blame this minister; I would rather today receive the offense of speaking fully than remain silent and bequeath regret.
translations.idiomatic: Later critics will blame me for my office—yet I would rather speak plainly now and accept the reproach than stay silent and leave regret behind.

sentences.zh: 」神宗納之，進為副使。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shenzong accepted this and promoted him to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice and promoted him to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 吳居厚為京東轉運使，數獻羨賦。

translations.literal: Wu Juho served as transport commissioner of Jingdong and repeatedly submitted surplus tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Juho, transport commissioner of Jingdong, repeatedly reported surplus revenues.

sentences.zh: 神宗將以徐州大錢二十萬緡助陝西，純粹語其僚曰：「吾部雖急，忍復取此膏血之餘？

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong was about to send two hundred thousand strings of large coin from Xuzhou to aid Shaanxi; Chun Cui told his staff: "Though my circuit is in straits, how can I bear to take again this remnant of the people's life's blood?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to send two hundred thousand strings of large cash from Xuzhou to support Shaanxi. Chun Cui told his staff, "My circuit is hard pressed—but how can we take what little remains of the people's sweat and blood?

sentences.zh: 」即奏：「本路得錢誠為利，自徐至邊，勞費甚矣。

translations.literal: " He at once memorialized: "For this circuit to receive the funds would indeed be profit, but from Xuzhou to the frontier the labor and expense would be very great.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized at once: "The money would help our circuit, but transporting it from Xuzhou to the border would cost more than it is worth.

sentences.zh: 」懇辭弗受。

translations.literal: " He earnestly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He declined firmly and refused the aid.

sentences.zh: 入為右司郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as director in the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as director in the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，居厚敗，命純粹以直龍圖閣往代之，盡革其苛政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, Juho fell from power; Chun Cui was ordered to go and replace him as Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Designs, entirely reforming his harsh policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong took the throne and Juho fell, Chun Cui was sent with the title Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Designs to replace him and thoroughly overturn his harsh measures.

sentences.zh: 時蘇軾自登州召還，純粹與軾同建募役之議，軾謂純粹講此事尤為精詳。

translations.literal: At the time Su Shi was recalled from Deng Prefecture; Chun Cui joined Shi in advancing the labor-exemption levy proposal, and Shi said Chun Cui's exposition of the matter was especially thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was recalled from Dengzhou, Chun Cui worked with him on the labor-exemption levy proposal. Su Shi said no one explained the matter more thoroughly than Chun Cui.

sentences.zh: 復代兄純仁知慶州。

translations.literal: He again replaced his elder brother Chunren as prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He again replaced his elder brother Chunren as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時與夏議分疆界，純粹請棄所取夏地，曰：「爭地未棄，則邊隙無時可除。

translations.literal: At the time they were negotiating border demarcation with Xia; Chun Cui requested abandonment of the Xia territory taken, saying: "Until disputed lands are abandoned, border friction can never be cleared away in time.
translations.idiomatic: While negotiating borders with Xia, Chun Cui urged giving back seized Xia territory: "Until we abandon the lands in dispute, border tensions will never end.

sentences.zh: 如河東之葭蘆、吳堡，鄜延之米脂、羲合、浮圖，環慶之安疆，深在夏境，於漢界地利形勢，略無所益。

translations.literal: Such places as Jialu and Wubao in Hedong, Mizhi, Yihe, and Futu in Yanyan, and Anjiang in Huanqing lie deep within Xia territory and for Han border terrain and strategic position are of almost no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Places like Jialu and Wubao in Hedong, Mizhi, Yihe, and Futu in Yanyan, and Anjiang in Huanqing lie deep in Xia territory and do the Song border almost no strategic good.

sentences.zh: 而蘭、會之地，耗蠹尤深，不可不棄。

translations.literal: As for the lands of Lan and Hui, the waste and drain are especially deep—they cannot but be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Lan and Hui territories are an especially costly drain and ought to be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 」所言皆略施行。

translations.literal: " What he said was all broadly put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: " His recommendations were largely adopted.

sentences.zh: 純粹又言：「諸路策應，舊制也。

translations.literal: Chun Cui further said: "Mutual support among circuits was the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Cui added: "Coordinated response among circuits was once standard practice.

sentences.zh: 自徐禧罷策應，若夏兵大舉，一路攻圍，力有不勝，而鄰路拱手坐觀，其不拔者幸爾。

translations.literal: Since Xu Xi abolished mutual support, if Xia troops come in force and one route is besieged and cannot prevail, neighboring routes fold their hands and sit watching—if the besieged are not taken it is only by luck.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xu Xi ended coordinated response, if Xia mounted a major attack one circuit could be overrun while its neighbors stood by. A successful defense would be mere luck.

sentences.zh: 今宜修明戰守救援之法。

translations.literal: Now one ought to clarify and restore methods of fighting, defending, and rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The methods of combat, defense, and mutual relief ought to be restored.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷是之。

translations.literal: " The court approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及夏侵涇原，純粹遣將曲珍救之，曰：「本道首建應援牽制之策，臣子之義，忘軀徇國，無謂鄰路被寇，非我職也。

translations.literal: When Xia invaded Jingyuan, Chun Cui sent the general Qu Zhen to the rescue, saying: "This circuit first devised the strategy of supporting and containing; the duty of a subject is to forget the body and devote oneself to the state. Do not say that when a neighboring route is attacked it is not my charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia invaded Jingyuan, Chun Cui sent General Qu Zhen to the rescue, saying: "This circuit pioneered the policy of diversionary relief. A loyal subject gives his life for the state. Do not say that a neighbor's attack is none of our business.

sentences.zh: 」珍即日疾馳三百里，破之于曲律，搗橫山，夏眾遁去。

translations.literal: " Zhen that same day galloped three hundred li, defeated the enemy at Qulu, raided Hengshan, and the Xia forces fled away.
translations.idiomatic: " Qu Zhen rode three hundred li that same day, routed the enemy at Qulu, struck Hengshan, and the Xia army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，除寶文閣待制，再任，召為戶部侍郎，又出知延州。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he was made Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, served a second term, was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue, and again sent out as prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou he was made Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, served a second term, was summoned as vice minister of revenue, and posted again as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shaosheng era.

sentences.zh: 哲宗親政，用事者欲開邊釁，御史郭知章遂論純粹元祐棄地事，降直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong took personal rule; those in power wished to open border provocation; censor Guo Zhizhang then attacked Chun Cui over the Yuanyou land abandonment and demoted him to Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Designs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong took direct control, the faction in power sought war on the frontier. Censor Guo Zhizhang attacked Chun Cui for surrendering territory during Yuanyou, and he was demoted to Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Designs.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以寶文閣待制知熙州。

translations.literal: The next year he was again made Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders and prefect of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was restored as Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders and prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 章惇、蔡卞經略西夏，疑純粹不與共事，改知鄧州。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun and Cai Bian were managing Western Xia affairs and suspected Chun Cui would not work with them; he was changed to prefect of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun and Cai Bian, directing policy toward Western Xia, doubted Chun Cui would cooperate and transferred him to prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 曆河南府、滑州，旋以元祐黨人奪職，知均州。

translations.literal: He served at Henan Prefecture and Hua Prefecture; soon, as a Yuanyou faction man, his office was stripped and he was made prefect of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Henan and Hua before being stripped of rank as a Yuanyou partisan and assigned to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，起知信州，復故職，知太原，加龍圖閣直學士，再臨延州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong acceded, he was raised to prefect of Xin Prefecture, restored to his former rank, made prefect of Taiyuan, given the additional title of Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs, and again took charge of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong acceded, Chun Cui was recalled as prefect of Xinzhou, restored to rank, made prefect of Taiyuan and Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs, and again posted to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 改知永興軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to commander of the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 尋以言者落職，知金州，提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Soon, on memorialists' attack, he lost office, was made prefect of Jin Prefecture, and administrator of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists soon stripped him of rank; he was made prefect of Jinzhou and administrator of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 又責常州別駕，鄂州安置，錮子弟不得擅入都。

translations.literal: He was further punished as vice prefect of Chang Prefecture, placed under restraint at E Prefecture, and his sons and younger brothers were barred from entering the capital without permission.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted to vice prefect of Changzhou, confined at Ezhou, and his sons and younger brothers were forbidden to enter the capital without leave.

sentences.zh: 會赦，復領祠。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came, he again received a sinecure post.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty restored him to a sinecure appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，以右文殿修撰提舉太清宮。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Compiler of the Hall of Right Culture and administrator of the Palace of Great Clarity.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Compiler of the Hall of Right Culture and administrator of the Palace of Great Clarity.

sentences.zh: 黨禁解，復徽猷閣待制，致仕。

translations.literal: When the faction ban was lifted, he was restored as Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Splendid Learning and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the faction ban ended he was restored as Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Splendid Learning and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-odd.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 純粹沉毅有幹略，才應時須，嘗論賣官之濫，以為：「國法固許進納取官，然未嘗聽其理選。

translations.literal: Chun Cui was deep, resolute, and capable in strategy; his talent met the needs of the time. He once discussed the abuse of selling offices, holding: "State law indeed permits gaining office through payment, yet never permitted their handling selection.
translations.idiomatic: Resolute and strategic, Chun Cui had the talents his age required. He once protested the abuse of selling offices: "The law allows purchase of rank, but never purchase of appointment by selection.

sentences.zh: 今西北三路，許納三千二百緡買齋郎，四千六百緡買供奉職，並免試注官。

translations.literal: Now on the three Northwestern routes one may pay three thousand two hundred strings to buy the rank of zailang, four thousand six hundred strings to buy palace attendant office, and both are exempt from examination and registered to office.
translations.idiomatic: On the three northwestern circuits, three thousand two hundred strings buys the rank of zailang and four thousand six hundred buys a palace attendant post—both without examination or vetting.

sentences.zh: 夫天下士大夫服勤至於垂死，不沾世恩，其富民猾商，捐錢千萬，則可任三子，切為朝廷惜之。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm scholars and officials serve diligently to their dying day yet receive no imperial favor; yet wealthy sharp merchants, donating ten million in cash, may place three sons in office—I deeply regret this for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars serve to their dying day without reward, while wealthy merchants who pay millions can place three sons in office. The court ought to cherish its dignity more than this.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，不聽。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " His memorial went in and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 凡論事剴切類此。

translations.literal: In general his policy discussions were incisive like this.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials on policy were characteristically this forthright.

sentences.zh: 范純仁

translations.literal: Fan Chunren
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunren

sentences.zh: 純仁，字堯夫，其始生之夕，母李氏夢兒墮月中，承以衣裾，得之，遂生純仁。

translations.literal: Chunren, styled Yaofu—on the night of his birth his mother Lady Li dreamed a child falling from the moon; she caught it in her robe's hem, received it, and thus Chunren was born.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren, styled Yaofu, was born on a night when his mother, Lady Li, dreamed of a child falling from the moon into the hem of her robe—and so he came into the world.

sentences.zh: 資警悟，八歲，能講所授書。

translations.literal: By nature quick to apprehend, at eight he could expound the books he was taught.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted from childhood, at eight he could lecture on his assigned texts.

sentences.zh: 以父任為太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: By his father's privilege he became libationer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he became libationer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 中皇祐元年進士第，調知武進縣，以遠親不赴；

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the first year of Huangyou, was assigned prefect of Wujin County, but did not take up the post because relatives were far away;
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Huangyou 1 and was assigned magistrate of Wujin County but declined because his kin were too far away;

sentences.zh: 易長葛，又不往。

translations.literal: the appointment was changed to Changge, and again he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: reassigned to Changge, he declined again.

sentences.zh: 仲淹曰：「汝昔日以遠為言，今近矣，復何辭？

translations.literal: Zhongyan said: "You once pleaded distance; now it is near—what excuse remains?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan said, "You pleaded distance before. Changge is near—what excuse do you have now?

sentences.zh: 」純仁曰：「豈可重於祿食，而輕去父母邪？

translations.literal: " Chunren said: "How can one weigh salary and rations more heavily and lightly leave one's parents?
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren replied, "How can I value salary above staying with my parents?

sentences.zh: 雖近，亦不能遂養焉。

translations.literal: Though near, I still cannot adequately support them.
translations.idiomatic: Even close by, I could not care for them properly.

sentences.zh: 」仲淹門下多賢士，如胡瑗、孫復、石介、李覯之徙，純仁皆與從遊。

translations.literal: " Under Zhongyan's gate were many worthy scholars, such as Hu Yuan, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, Li Gou, and the like; Chunren all followed and studied with them.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongyan's circle included men like Hu Yuan, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, and Li Gou, and Chunren studied among them all.

sentences.zh: 晝夜肄業，至夜分不寢，置燈帳中，帳頂如墨色。

translations.literal: Day and night he pursued his studies; until midnight he did not sleep, placing the lamp inside his curtain, the top of the curtain like ink in color.
translations.idiomatic: He studied day and night, not sleeping until after midnight; the lamp in his bed-curtain stained the fabric above black with soot.

sentences.zh: 仲俺沒，始出仕，以著作佐郎知襄城縣。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan died, he first entered office, as editorial assistant and magistrate of Xiangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Zhongyan's death did he take office, as editorial assistant and magistrate of Xiangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 兄純祐有心疾，奉之如父，藥膳居服，皆躬親時節之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chunyou had a heart illness; he served him as a father—medicine, food, lodging, and mourning observances he all personally attended at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chunyou suffered a mental disorder; Chunren cared for him as for a father, personally tending his medicine, meals, lodging, and mourning rites at every season.

sentences.zh: 賈昌朝守北都，請參幕府，以兄辭。

translations.literal: Jia Changchao held the Northern Capital and invited him to join his staff; he declined on account of his brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Changchao governed the Northern Capital he asked Chunren to join his staff; Chunren declined for his brother's sake.

sentences.zh: 宋庠薦試館職，謝曰：「輦轂之下，非兄養疾地也。

translations.literal: Song Xiang recommended him for examination for an academy post; he declined, saying: "Beneath the imperial carriage-hub is not a place for my brother to convalesce.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xiang recommended him for an academy examination. He declined: "The capital is no place to nurse my brother's illness.

sentences.zh: 」富弼責之曰：「臺閣之任豈易得？

translations.literal: " Fu Bi rebuked him, saying: "Is an appointment to the Censorate and Institute so easily obtained?
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Bi scolded him: "Do you think a post at court comes so easily?

sentences.zh: 何庸如是。

translations.literal: Why must you be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Why waste an opportunity like this?

sentences.zh: 」卒不就。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He never accepted.

sentences.zh: 襄城民不蠶織，勸使植桑，有罪而情輕者，視所植多寡除其罰，民益賴慕，後呼為「著作林」。

translations.literal: The people of Xiangcheng did not raise silkworms or weave; he urged them to plant mulberry. For offenders whose guilt was light, he remitted punishment according to how much mulberry they had planted; the people increasingly relied on and admired him, and later called him "Editorial Assistant Lin."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiangcheng did not raise silkworms; he urged mulberry planting and, for minor offenders, reduced fines according to trees planted. They came to trust and admire him, calling him "Editorial Assistant of the Grove."

sentences.zh: 兄死，葬洛陽。

translations.literal: When his brother died, he was buried in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After his brother died, Chunren buried him in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 韓琦、富弼貽書洛尹，使助其葬，既葬，尹訝不先聞。

translations.literal: Han Qi and Fu Bi sent letters to the Luoyang prefect asking him to assist with the burial; after the burial the prefect wondered that he had not been told beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and Fu Bi wrote the Luoyang prefect asking him to help with the funeral. After the burial the prefect was surprised he had not been told in advance.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「私室力足辦，豈宜慁公為哉？」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "My private household had sufficient means to manage it—how could it be right to trouble your lordship?"
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Our family could manage it ourselves. Why should we have imposed on you?"

sentences.zh: 簽書許州觀察判官、知襄邑縣。

translations.literal: He signed as administrative assistant to the military commissioner of Xuzhou and served as magistrate of Xiangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy administrator of Xuzhou and magistrate of Xiangyi County.

sentences.zh: 縣有牧地，衛士牧馬，以踐民稼，純仁捕一人杖之。

translations.literal: The county had pasture land; imperial guards pastured horses there and trampled the people's crops; Chunren seized one man and had him beaten with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial guards pastured horses on county pastureland and trampled crops; Chunren seized one man and had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 牧地初不隸縣，主者怒曰：「天子宿衛，令敢爾邪？

translations.literal: The pasture had not originally been under county jurisdiction; its overseer angrily said: "They are the Son of Heaven's palace guards—you, magistrate, dare do such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: The pasture was not under county jurisdiction. Its overseer raged: "These are the emperor's own guards—how dare a county magistrate do this?

sentences.zh: 」白其事於上，劾治甚急。

translations.literal: " He reported the matter above and pressed for prosecution with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: " He reported the matter to the throne and demanded severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「養兵出於稅畝，若使暴民田而不得問，稅安所出？

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Maintaining troops comes from tax grain per mu; if they ravage the people's fields and nothing may be asked, whence will taxes come?
translations.idiomatic: Chunren replied, "Armies are fed from the fields. If soldiers may trample farmland with impunity, where will taxes come from?

sentences.zh: 」詔釋之，且聽牧地隸縣。

translations.literal: " An edict released him and moreover permitted pasture lands to fall under county jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict freed him and allowed pasture lands to be placed under county authority.

sentences.zh: 凡牧地隸縣，自純仁始。

translations.literal: In general, making pasture lands fall under counties began with Chunren.
translations.idiomatic: County jurisdiction over pasture lands began with Chunren.

sentences.zh: 時旱久不雨，純仁籍境內賈舟，諭之曰：「民將無食，爾所販五穀，貯之佛寺，候食闕時吾為糴之。

translations.literal: At the time drought had long gone without rain; Chunren registered merchant boats within the jurisdiction and instructed them: "The people will soon have no food; store the grain you trade in Buddhist temples, and when food runs short I will buy it from you.
translations.idiomatic: During a prolonged drought Chunren registered merchant boats in his jurisdiction and told them, "People will soon go hungry. Store your grain in Buddhist temples; when food runs short I will buy it from you.

sentences.zh: 」眾賈從命，所蓄十數萬斛。

translations.literal: " The merchants all obeyed; what they stored amounted to several hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: " The merchants complied, stockpiling more than a hundred thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 至春，諸縣皆饑，獨境內民不知也。

translations.literal: When spring came, all counties were famine-stricken; only within his jurisdiction did the people not know it.
translations.idiomatic: That spring neighboring counties starved, while people in his jurisdiction scarcely knew famine had come.

sentences.zh: 治平中，擢江東轉運判官，召為殿中侍御史，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era he was promoted transport vice commissioner of Jiangdong, summoned as palace censor, and transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiping he was promoted Jiangdong transport vice commissioner, then summoned as palace censor and elevated to full censor.

sentences.zh: 時方議濮王典禮，宰相韓琦、參知政事歐陽修等議尊崇之。

translations.literal: At the time they were debating the rites due to Prince Pu; chancellor Han Qi, Vice Grand Councilor Ouyang Xiu, and others argued for honoring him loftily.
translations.idiomatic: The court was debating rites for Prince Pu. Chancellor Han Qi, Vice Grand Councilor Ouyang Xiu, and others favored granting him the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士王珪等議，宜如先朝追贈期親尊屬故事。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others argued it should follow the precedent of former dynasties in posthumously ennobling close senior relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others argued for the precedent of posthumously ennobling close senior kin as in earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「陛下受命仁宗而為之子，與前代定策入繼之主異，宜如王珪等議。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Your Majesty received the mandate from Renzong and became his son—different from former emperors who entered the succession by fixing the design; it should be as Wang Gui and others propose.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren argued, "Your Majesty took the throne from Renzong as his son—not like earlier emperors who entered by coup. Wang Gui's view is the right one.

sentences.zh: 」繼與御史呂誨等更論奏，不聽。

translations.literal: " He continued with censor Lü Hui and others to submit further memorials; they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " He and censors including Lü Hui memorialized repeatedly; the throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 純仁還所授告敕，家居待罪。

translations.literal: Chunren returned the patents of appointment he had received and remained at home awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren returned his commissions and stayed home awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 既而皇太后手書尊王為皇，夫人為後。

translations.literal: Soon the empress dowager by her own hand wrote to honor the prince as emperor and his consort as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager then issued a handwritten edict making the prince emperor and his consort empress.

sentences.zh: 純仁復言：「陛下以長君臨禦，奈何使命出房闈，異日或為權臣矯托之地，非人主自安計。

translations.literal: Chunren again said: "Your Majesty as adult sovereign holds court—how can commands issue from the inner quarters? In days to come this may become ground for powerful ministers to forge and borrow authority—not a plan by which a ruler secures his own ease.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren protested again: "Your Majesty rules in your own right. Orders ought not to come from the women's quarters lest someday powerful ministers use them as cover for forgery. That is no way for a sovereign to secure his position.

sentences.zh: 」尋詔罷追尊，起純仁就職。

translations.literal: " Soon an edict halted the posthumous elevation and raised Chunren to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon an edict halted the posthumous honors and Chunren was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 純仁請出不已，遂通判安州，改知蘄州。

translations.literal: Chunren requested to leave office without cease; he was then made vice prefect of Anzhou and transferred to prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren kept asking to leave court; he was finally made vice prefect of Anzhou, then prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 曆京西提點刑獄、京西陝西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Jingxi judicial intendant and Jingxi-Shaanxi transport vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial intendant for Jingxi, then as Jingxi-Shaanxi transport vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召還，神宗問陝西城郭、甲兵、糧儲如何，對曰：「城郭粗全，甲兵粗修，糧儲粗備。

translations.literal: He was recalled. Shenzong asked how Shaanxi's fortifications, armor and troops, and grain stores were. He replied: "The fortifications are roughly intact, armor and troops roughly repaired, grain stores roughly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, Shenzong asked about Shaanxi's walls, arms, and granaries. Chunren answered, "The walls are more or less intact, arms more or less ready, stores more or less full.

sentences.zh: 」神宗愕然曰：「卿之才朕所倚信，何為皆言粗？

translations.literal: " Shenzong said in astonishment: "Your talent is what I rely upon and trust—why do you speak of everything as 'rough'?
translations.idiomatic: " Shenzong was taken aback. "I trust your judgment completely. Why do you describe everything as merely adequate?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「粗者未精之辭，如是足矣。

translations.literal: " He replied: "'Rough' is language for 'not yet refined'—this much is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "By 'rough' I mean adequate, not perfect—and that is enough.

sentences.zh: 願陛下且無留意邊功，若邊臣觀望，將為他日意外之患。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will for now not fix your mind on frontier achievements; if frontier officials wait and watch, it will become an unforeseen trouble on another day.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty not to fixate on frontier victories. If border officials hang back in caution, that will breed unexpected trouble later.

sentences.zh: 」拜兵部員外郎，兼起居舍人、同知諫院。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Vice Minister of War, concurrently diarist-recorder and co-director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Vice Minister of War, also serving as diarist and associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「王安石變祖宗法度，掊克財利，民心不寧。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Wang Anshi has altered the ancestral laws and institutions, extorted wealth and profit, and the people's hearts are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Wang Anshi had overturned ancestral institutions, squeezed the people for revenue, and left the realm uneasy.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：'怨豈在明，不見是圖。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'Resentment is not only in what is visible—attend to what is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, 'Grievance lies not only in what is plain to see—heed what remains unseen.'

sentences.zh: '願陛下圖不見之怨。

translations.literal: ' I hope Your Majesty will address resentment that is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to heed the grievances no one speaks aloud.

sentences.zh: 」神宗曰：「何謂不見之怨？

translations.literal: " Shenzong said: "What is meant by resentment that is not seen?
translations.idiomatic: " Shenzong asked, "What grievances do you mean—ones that are unseen?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「杜牧所謂'天下之人，不敢言而敢怒'是也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "It is as Du Mu said: 'All under Heaven dare not speak yet dare to rage.'
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Du Mu put it best: 'The people under Heaven dare not speak out—but they dare to seethe with anger.'

sentences.zh: 」神宗嘉納之，曰：「卿善論事，宜為朕條古今治亂可為監戒者。

translations.literal: " Shenzong praised and accepted this, saying: "You discuss affairs well—you should draw up for me examples from antiquity and present of order and disorder that may serve as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenzong approved heartily. "You argue well. Compile for me from history lessons in good government and ruin that may serve as warnings.

sentences.zh: 」乃作《尚書解》以進，曰：「其言，皆堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之事也。

translations.literal: " He then composed A Commentary on the Documents and presented it, saying: "Its words are all the affairs of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted his Commentary on the Documents, writing, "Every passage concerns the deeds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu.

sentences.zh: 治天下無以易此，願深究而力行之。

translations.literal: To govern All under Heaven nothing can replace this; I hope you will deeply investigate and vigorously carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: There is no better model for governing the realm. I pray Your Majesty will study it deeply and put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 」加直集賢院、同修起居注。

translations.literal: " He was additionally appointed academy diarist of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and co-compiler of the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: " He was further appointed academy diarist of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and co-compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 神宗切於求治，多延見疏逖小臣，咨訪闕失。

translations.literal: Shenzong was eager in seeking good governance, often extending audiences to distant and minor officials, consulting on lapses and errors.
translations.idiomatic: Eager for reform, Shenzong often summoned obscure junior officials to ask where the government had fallen short.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「小人之言，聽之若可采，行之必有累。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "The words of petty men—hearing them they seem adoptable, but carrying them out will surely bring burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren warned, "Petty men's advice often sounds plausible at first, yet always brings harm in execution.

sentences.zh: 蓋知小忘大，貪近昧遠，願加深察。

translations.literal: For they know the small and forget the large, grasp what is near and blur what is far—I hope for deeper scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: They fixate on small gains and lose sight of the whole, chase what is near and blind themselves to distant consequences. I urge deeper scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 」富弼在相位，稱疾家居。

translations.literal: " While Fu Bi held the chancellorship, he claimed illness and remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Bi had been chancellor but was now at home feigning illness.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「弼受三朝眷倚，當自任天下之重，而恤己深於恤物，憂疾過於憂邦，致主處身，二者胥失。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Bi received the favor and reliance of three reigns—he ought to take upon himself the weight of All under Heaven, yet he pities himself more than he pities others, and grieves over his illness more than he grieves over the state—in serving his lord and conducting himself personally, both are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren wrote, "Three reigns trusted Fu Bi. He ought to bear the weight of the realm—but he pities himself more than the people, frets over his health more than the state. In serving his sovereign and in his own conduct, he has failed on both counts.

sentences.zh: 弼與先臣素厚，臣在諫省，不錄私謁以致忠告，願示以此章，使之自省。

translations.literal: Bi and my late father were always close; I am in the Remonstrance Bureau and did not record a private visit so as to offer loyal counsel—I hope this memorial may be shown to him so that he may examine himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi was close to my late father. As a remonstrance official I avoided a private audience to give this candid advice. I ask that this memorial be shown him, that he may reflect on himself.

sentences.zh: 」又論呂誨不當罷御史中丞，李師中不可守邊。

translations.literal: " He also argued that Lü Hui should not have been dismissed as censor-in-chief, and that Li Shizhong was unsuitable to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " He also argued against removing Lü Hui as chief censor and against posting Li Shizhong on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及薛向任發運使，行均輸法于六路。

translations.literal: When Xue Xiang was appointed grain transport commissioner, he implemented the equal-transport law in the six circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Xiang became grain transport commissioner, he imposed the equal-transport system across six circuits.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「臣嘗親奉德音，欲修先王補助之政。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Your servant once personally received Your virtuous decree, wishing to restore the assisting policies of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren protested, "I once heard Your Majesty's own words: you wished to restore the former kings' policy of aiding the people.

sentences.zh: 今乃效桑羊均輸之法，而使小人為之，掊克生靈，斂怨基禍。

translations.literal: Now you imitate Sang Hongyang's equal-transport method and leave petty men to carry it out—extorting from the living, gathering resentment and laying foundations for calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Now you copy Sang Hongyang's equal-transport scheme and leave it to petty men. They squeeze the people, breed resentment, and lay up disaster.

sentences.zh: 安石以富國強兵之術，啟迪上心，欲求近功，忘其舊學。

translations.literal: Anshi used arts of enriching the state and strengthening the army to enlighten the emperor's heart, seeking near-term achievement and forgetting his former learning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi dazzles the throne with schemes to enrich the state and strengthen the army. Eager for quick results, he has abandoned his own learning.

sentences.zh: 尚法令則稱商鞅，言財利則背孟軻，鄙老成為因循，棄公論為流俗，異己者為不肖，合意者為賢人。

translations.literal: When honoring laws and ordinances he cites Lord Shang; when speaking of wealth and profit he turns his back on Mencius; he despises seasoned officials as stuck in routine, rejects public opinion as vulgar custom, treats dissenters as unworthy, and treats those who agree with him as worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: He cites Lord Shang when praising harsh law, abandons Mencius when money is at stake, scorns experienced men as hidebound, dismisses honest debate as vulgar opinion, calls dissenters worthless and flatterers wise.

sentences.zh: 劉琦、錢顗等一言，便蒙降黜。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, Qian Yi, and others—for a single word they at once suffered demotion and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi, Qian Yi, and others were demoted for a single remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 在廷之臣，方大半趨附。

translations.literal: Officials at court were then mostly rushing to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials at court were already scrambling to fall in line.

sentences.zh: 陛下又從而驅之，其將何所不至。

translations.literal: Your Majesty again drives them on from behind—where will this not reach?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty drives them further still. Where will it end?

sentences.zh: 道遠者理當馴致，事大者不可速成，人材不可急求，積敝不可頓革。

translations.literal: What is distant in the Way should by right be brought near step by step; great affairs cannot be quickly completed; talent cannot be urgently sought; accumulated ills cannot be suddenly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Distant goals must be approached gradually. Great undertakings cannot be rushed to completion. Talent cannot be forced into being overnight. Deep-rooted evils cannot be uprooted at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 儻欲事功亟就，必為憸佞所乘，宜速還言者而退安石，答中外之望。

translations.literal: If you wish achievement to be completed hastily, you will surely be taken advantage of by the sly and fawning—you should quickly restore the remonstrators and remove Anshi, answering the hopes of within and without.
translations.idiomatic: If you rush for results, sycophants will exploit the moment. Restore the remonstrators and dismiss Wang Anshi—that is what the court and the country expect.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂求罷諫職，改判國子監，去意愈確。

translations.literal: He then requested dismissal from remonstrance duties, was transferred to director of the Directorate of Education, and his intent to leave grew more firm.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave the Remonstrance Bureau and was reassigned to head the Directorate of Education, his resolve to quit growing firmer.

sentences.zh: 執政使諭之曰：「毋輕去，已議除知制誥矣。

translations.literal: The chief ministers sent someone to instruct him: "Do not leave lightly—we have already discussed appointing you drafting-compiler of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers sent word: "Do not be so quick to go. We have already discussed making you drafting compiler of edicts.

sentences.zh: 」純仁曰：「此言何為至於我哉，言不用，萬鐘非所顧也。」

translations.literal: " Chunren said: "Why should such words be directed at me? If my words are not used, ten thousand piculs are not what I care for."
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren replied, "Why address such talk to me? If my counsel goes unheeded, even the highest office holds no appeal."

sentences.zh: 其所上章疏，語多激切。

translations.literal: The memorials he submitted—in their language there was much that was sharp and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were often sharp and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 神宗悉不付外，純仁盡錄申中書，安石大怒，乞加重貶。

translations.literal: Shenzong sent none of them outside; Chunren copied them all and submitted them to the Secretariat. Anshi was greatly angered and requested heavier demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong kept them all internal, but Chunren copied every one and sent them to the Secretariat. Wang Anshi was furious and demanded a heavier punishment.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「彼無罪，姑與一善地。

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "He is without guilt—for now give him a good post.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said, "He has committed no crime. Give him a decent post for now.

sentences.zh: 」命知河中府，徙成都路轉運使。

translations.literal: " He was ordered prefect of Hezhong prefecture, then transferred to Chengdu circuit transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made prefect of Hezhong, then transferred to Chengdu circuit transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以新法不便，戒州縣未得遽行。

translations.literal: Because the new laws were inconvenient, he ordered prefectures and counties not to rush implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the new laws burdensome, he warned counties and prefectures not to implement them hastily.

sentences.zh: 安石怒純仁沮格，因讒者遣使欲捃摭私事，不能得。

translations.literal: Anshi was angry that Chunren obstructed and blocked; through slanderers he sent envoys wishing to gather and expose private matters, but could not obtain any.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, furious at Chunren's obstruction, sent agents through informers to dig up private wrongdoing but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 使者以他事鞭傷傳言者，屬官喜謂純仁曰：「此一事足以塞其謗，請聞於朝。

translations.literal: The envoy for another matter whipped and injured a messenger; a subordinate official rejoiced and said to Chunren: "This one matter is enough to block their slander—please report it to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy whipped a messenger over another matter, a subordinate exulted and told Chunren, "This incident alone can silence the slanderers. Report it to court.

sentences.zh: 」純仁既不奏使者之過，亦不折言者之非。

translations.literal: " Chunren neither memorialized the envoy's fault, nor rebuked the messenger's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren neither reported the envoy's abuse nor scolded the messenger for his error.

sentences.zh: 後竟坐失察僚佐燕游，左遷知和州，徙邢州。

translations.literal: Later he was finally punished for failure to supervise subordinates' feasting and carousing, demoted to prefect of Hezhou, then transferred to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually demoted for failing to restrain subordinates' revelry—first to Hezhou, then Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，加直龍圖閣、知慶州。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, he was additionally appointed Dragon Diagram Hall academician diarist and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, he was made Dragon Diagram Hall academician and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 過闕入對，神宗曰：「卿父在慶著威名，今可謂世職。

translations.literal: Passing the palace gate he entered audience. Shenzong said: "Your father at Qingzhou won a famous reputation for authority—today this may be called a hereditary post.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned before the throne, Shenzong said, "Your father made a great name defending Qingzhou. This is almost a family post.

sentences.zh: 卿隨父既久，兵法必精，邊事必熟。

translations.literal: You followed your father so long—your art of war must be skilled, frontier affairs must be familiar.
translations.idiomatic: You served beside him for years. Surely you know tactics and the border well.

sentences.zh: 」純仁揣神宗有功名心，即對曰：「臣儒家，未嘗學兵，先臣守邊時，臣尚幼，不復記憶，且今日事勢宜有不同。

translations.literal: " Chunren guessed Shenzong had a heart for achievement and fame, and immediately replied: "Your servant is of the Ru school and has never studied war; when my late father guarded the frontier I was still young and no longer remember—and besides, today's situation ought to differ.
translations.idiomatic: " Sensing Shenzong's thirst for glory, Chunren answered at once, "I am a Confucian scholar, never trained in war. I was still a boy when my father served on the frontier and remember little—and today's situation calls for different measures anyway.

sentences.zh: 陛下使臣繕治城壘，愛養百姓，不敢辭；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty sends me to repair walls and ramparts and cherish and nurture the people, I dare not decline;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wants me to repair the walls and care for the people, I will not refuse;

sentences.zh: 若開拓侵攘，願別謀帥臣。

translations.literal: if it is expansion, invasion, and encroachment, I hope another commander may be found.
translations.idiomatic: but for conquest and aggression, please find another commander.

sentences.zh: 」神宗曰：「卿之才何所不能，顧不肯為朕悉心爾。

translations.literal: " Shenzong said: "Your talent—what can you not do? You simply will not devote yourself wholeheartedly for me.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenzong said, "Your abilities know no limit. You simply refuse to give yourself fully to me.

sentences.zh: 」遂行。

translations.literal: " He then departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren took up the post.

sentences.zh: 秦中方饑，擅發常平粟振貸。

translations.literal: Shaanxi was then in famine; without authorization he released ever-normal granary grain for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Shaanxi; without waiting for permission he opened the ever-normal granaries to lend grain to the starving.

sentences.zh: 僚屬請奏而須報，純仁曰：「報至無及矣，吾當獨任其責。

translations.literal: Subordinates asked to memorialize and await reply. Chunren said: "By the time the reply arrives it will be too late—I shall alone bear the responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Staff urged him to memorialize and wait for approval. Chunren said, "By then it will be too late. I alone will accept the blame.

sentences.zh: 」或謗其所全活不實，詔遣使按視。

translations.literal: " Some slandered that those he had fully saved and kept alive were not as reported; an edict sent envoys to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: " When slanderers claimed he had inflated the number saved, the court sent investigators.

sentences.zh: 會秋大稔，民歡曰：「公實活我，忍累公邪？

translations.literal: It happened that autumn brought great abundance; the people rejoiced and said: "The lord truly kept us alive—can we bear to burden the lord?
translations.idiomatic: That autumn brought a bumper harvest. Grateful people cried, "You truly saved us—how can we let you suffer for it?

sentences.zh: 」晝夜爭輸還之。

translations.literal: " Day and night they vied to return what they had received.
translations.idiomatic: " Day and night they rushed to repay what they owed.

sentences.zh: 使者至，已無所負。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, there was nothing still owed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time investigators arrived, every loan had been repaid.

sentences.zh: 邠、甯間有叢塚，使者曰：「全活不實之罪，於此得矣。

translations.literal: Between Bin and Ning there were clustered tombs. The envoy said: "The crime of falsely reporting those saved and kept alive—here it is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Between Bin and Ning stood clusters of graves. The envoy declared, "Here's proof he lied about how many he saved.

sentences.zh: 」發塚籍骸上之。

translations.literal: " They opened the tombs and registered the bones and sent them up.
translations.idiomatic: " They opened the graves, catalogued the bones, and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 詔本路監司窮治，乃前帥楚建中所封也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered route supervisory officials to investigate thoroughly—it turned out to be tombs sealed by the former commander Chu Jianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors were ordered to investigate—and learned the graves had been sealed by Chunren's predecessor, Chu Jianzhong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷治建中罪，純仁上疏言：「建中守法，申請間不免有殍死者，已坐罪罷去。

translations.literal: The court prosecuted Jianzhong for crime. Chunren submitted a memorial saying: "Jianzhong observed the law; in the interval of applying and requesting, unavoidably there were those who died of starvation—he has already been punished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to punish Chu Jianzhong, Chunren memorialized, "Jianzhong obeyed the law. People still starved while he waited for approval. He was already punished and removed.

sentences.zh: 今緣按臣而及建中，是一罪再刑也。

translations.literal: Now because of investigating me they reach Jianzhong—this is one crime punished twice.
translations.idiomatic: Now he faces punishment again simply because of the inquiry into me. That is punishing the same offense twice.

sentences.zh: 」建中猶贖銅三十斤。

translations.literal: " Jianzhong still had to redeem with thirty jin of copper.
