translations.idiomatic: " Jianzhong was still fined thirty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 環州種古執熟羌為盜，流南方，過慶呼冤，純仁以屬吏，非盜也。

translations.literal: At Huanzhou, Zhong Gu seized settled Di people as thieves and exiled them to the south; passing through Qing they cried out their innocence. Chunren entrusted it to subordinate officials—it was not theft.
translations.idiomatic: At Huanzhou, Zhong Gu had arrested settled Qiang as bandits and sent them south. Passing through Qingzhou they pleaded innocence. Chunren delegated the case—and they were found innocent.

sentences.zh: 古避罪讕訟，詔御史治于寧州。

translations.literal: Gu, to avoid guilt, falsely accused and litigated; an edict ordered censors to try the case at Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu tried to evade blame with false counter-charges. Censors were ordered to try the case at Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 純仁就逮，民萬數遮馬涕泗，不得行，至有自投於河者。

translations.literal: Chunren was taken into custody; tens of thousands of people blocked his horse with tears, and he could not proceed—some even threw themselves into the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunren was arrested, ten thousand people blocked his horse in tears; he could not move forward. Some threw themselves into the river.

sentences.zh: 獄成，古以誣告謫。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, Gu was demoted for false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: When the trial ended, Gu was demoted for false accusation.

sentences.zh: 亦加純仁以他過，黜知信陽軍。

translations.literal: They also added other faults to Chunren and dismissed him to prefect of Xinyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren was also punished on other grounds and demoted to military prefect of Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 移齊州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 齊俗兇悍，人輕為盜劫。

translations.literal: Qi's customs were fierce and violent; people lightly committed robbery and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhou had a fierce reputation; robbery was common.

sentences.zh: 或謂：「此嚴治之猶不能戢，公一以寬，恐不勝其治矣。

translations.literal: Some said: "Even with strict governance this cannot be restrained—you alone apply leniency; I fear you will not be equal to governing it.
translations.idiomatic: Some warned, "Even harsh rule barely restrains these people. If you govern with leniency alone, I fear the district will overwhelm you.

sentences.zh: 」純仁曰：「寬出於性，若強以猛，則不能持久；

translations.literal: " Chunren said: "Leniency comes from my nature; if I force harshness, it cannot last;
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren replied, "Gentleness is my nature. Forced severity cannot last;

sentences.zh: 猛而不久，以治凶民，取玩之道也。

translations.literal: harshness without duration—using this to govern violent people is the way to invite contempt.
translations.idiomatic: short-lived harshness against violent people invites only contempt.

sentences.zh: 」有西司理院，系囚常滿，皆屠販盜竊而督償者。

translations.literal: " There was a western judicial detention yard; prisoners were always full—it was all butchers, peddlers, petty thieves pursued for repayment of debts.
translations.idiomatic: " The western judicial yard was always packed with butchers, peddlers, and petty thieves held until they paid their debts.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「此何不保外使輸納邪？

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Why not release them on bail outside and have them pay in installments?
translations.idiomatic: Chunren asked, "Why not release them on bail to pay in installments?

sentences.zh: 」通判曰：「此釋之，復紊，官司往往待其以疾斃於獄中，是與民除害爾。

translations.literal: " The vice prefect said: "If these are released, disorder returns—the offices often wait for them to die of illness in prison—that is removing harm for the people.
translations.idiomatic: " The vice prefect said, "Release them and crime surges again. Officials often let debtors die in jail—that's how they 'protect' the people.

sentences.zh: 」純仁曰：「法不至死，以情殺之，豈理也邪？

translations.literal: " Chunren said: "The law does not reach death—to kill by feeling, is this principle?
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren said, "The law does not prescribe death. To kill by whim—is that justice?

sentences.zh: 」盡呼至庭下，訓使自新，即釋去。

translations.literal: " He summoned them all to the courtyard, admonished them to reform themselves, and immediately released them.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned them all, admonished them to reform, and released them at once.

sentences.zh: 期歲，盜減比年大半。

translations.literal: Within a year, robbery decreased by more than half compared with recent years.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, crime fell by more than half.

sentences.zh: 丐罷，提舉西京留司御史台。

translations.literal: He requested dismissal and was appointed to oversee the Western Capital residual Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to step down and was made overseer of the Western Capital residual Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時耆賢多在洛，純仁及司馬光，皆好客而家貧，相約為真率會，脫粟一飯，酒數行，洛中以為勝事。

translations.literal: At the time many worthy elders were mostly in Luoyang. Chunren and Sima Guang were both fond of guests yet poor; they agreed on a "Plain Sincerity Gathering"—plain millet for one meal, wine for a few rounds—Luoyang considered it a fine affair.
translations.idiomatic: Many eminent men then lived in Luoyang. Chunren and Sima Guang, both hospitable but poor, formed a "Plain Sincerity Society"—a meal of plain millet, a few cups of wine. Luoyang judged it the finest entertainment in town.

sentences.zh: 復知河中，諸路閱保甲妨農，論救甚力。

translations.literal: Again made prefect of Hezhong; on routes reviewing the baojia militia that hampered farming, he argued for relief with great force.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Hezhong again and argued forcefully that baojia militia drills were ruining the harvest.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍宋儋年暴死，純仁使子弟視喪，小殮，口鼻血出。

translations.literal: Recorder-assistant Song Danian died suddenly. Chunren sent his sons to view the mourning; at minor encoffining, blood came from mouth and nose.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Song Danian died suddenly. When Chunren's sons went to view the body at encoffining, blood seeped from mouth and nose.

sentences.zh: 純仁疑其非命，按得其妾與小吏奸，因會，寘毒鱉肉中。

translations.literal: Chunren suspected unnatural death; investigation found his concubine and a petty clerk in adultery—they had at a gathering placed poison in turtle meat.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren suspected foul play and found the concubine and a clerk were lovers. At a feast they had poisoned turtle meat.

sentences.zh: 純仁問食肉在第幾巡，曰：「豈有既中毒而尚能終席者乎？

translations.literal: Chunren asked at which round of the meat he had eaten, and said: "How could one already poisoned still finish the banquet?
translations.idiomatic: Chunren asked which course of the feast Danian had eaten from. "Could a poisoned man sit through the whole banquet?

sentences.zh: 」再訊之，則儋年素不食鱉，其曰毒鱉肉者，蓋妾與吏欲為變獄張本，以逃死爾。

translations.literal: " Questioning again, it turned out Danian had never eaten turtle; their saying poison turtle meat was likely the concubine and clerk wishing to lay groundwork for altering the case to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: " Further questioning revealed Danian never ate turtle. The turtle story was the concubine and clerk laying groundwork to overturn the case and escape execution.

sentences.zh: 實儋年醉歸，毒於酒而殺之。

translations.literal: In fact Danian returned drunk; they poisoned the wine and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In truth Danian came home drunk—they killed him with poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 遂正其罪。

translations.literal: Their guilt was then established.
translations.idiomatic: Their guilt was established and they were punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，復直龍圖閣、知慶州。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended, he was again made Dragon Diagram Hall academician diarist and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne, Chunren was again made Dragon Diagram Hall academician and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為右諫議大夫，以親嫌辭，改天章閣待制兼侍講，除給事中。

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Remonstrance Grand Master; citing kinship disqualification he declined, was changed to Hanlin Academy attendant compiler and concurrent lecturer, then appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Right Remonstrance Grand Master, he declined citing kinship disqualification, was made Hanlin attendant compiler and lecturer, then appointed Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時宣仁後垂簾，司馬光為政，將盡改熙甯、元豐法度。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Xuanren held the curtain behind the throne; Sima Guang held power and was about to entirely change the Xining and Yuanfeng laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager Xuanren was regent and Sima Guang governed, set on overturning every Xining and Yuanfeng reform.

sentences.zh: 純仁謂光：「去其太甚者可也。

translations.literal: Chunren said to Guang: "Removing what is too excessive would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren told Guang, "Repeal only the worst excesses.

sentences.zh: 差役一事，尤當熟講而緩行，不然，滋為民病。

translations.literal: On the matter of corvée service replacement especially careful discussion and slow implementation are needed; otherwise it will increasingly become a hardship for the people.
translations.idiomatic: On corvée reform especially, debate thoroughly and move slowly—or it will only multiply the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: 願公虛心以延眾論，不必謀自己出；

translations.literal: I hope you will with empty mind extend audience to public discussion—not necessarily plotting that plans come from yourself;
translations.idiomatic: Keep an open mind and welcome debate. Plans need not all originate with you;

sentences.zh: 謀自己出，則諂諛得乘間迎合矣。

translations.literal: if plans come from yourself, then flattery and sycophancy can seize the interval to match and accommodate.
translations.idiomatic: if every plan is yours alone, flatterers will seize the chance to tell you what you want to hear.

sentences.zh: 役議或難回，則可先行之一路，以觀其究竟。

translations.literal: If the corvée proposal is hard to turn back, then it may first be implemented in one circuit to observe its ultimate outcome.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot reconsider corvée reform, test it in one circuit first and see how it ends.

sentences.zh: 」光不從，持之益豎。

translations.literal: " Guang did not follow this; he held to his view ever more rigidly.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang would not listen and dug in all the harder.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「是使人不得言爾。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "This simply keeps people from speaking."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "That only silences people."

sentences.zh: 若欲媚公以為容悅，何如少年合安石以速富貴哉。

translations.literal: If one wished to flatter you for favor and delight, how much better for a young man to attach himself to Anshi for quick wealth and rank!
translations.idiomatic: If I wanted to flatter you for approval, I might have joined Wang Anshi as a young man and raced toward power and wealth.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「熙寧按問自首之法，既已行之，有司立文太深，四方死者視舊數倍，殆非先王寧失不經之意。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Xining law on interrogation and voluntary confession, once implemented, led officials to draft regulations too harshly; dead across the four quarters were several times the old count—hardly the former kings' intent that it is better to let the innocent go than to punish without cause.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The Xining law on interrogation and voluntary confession has been in force, yet officials drafted rules so harsh that deaths across the realm multiplied severalfold. That can hardly accord with the ancient principle that it is better to let the guilty go than to punish the innocent.

sentences.zh: 」純仁素與光同志，及臨事規正，類如此。

translations.literal: " Chunren had always shared Guang's views, yet when events arose he corrected them—mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren had always been allied with Sima Guang, yet when matters came to a head he spoke up to correct him—again and again.

sentences.zh: 初，種古因誣純仁停任。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhong Gu had been suspended from office for falsely accusing Chunren.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhong Gu had been removed from office for falsely accusing Chunren.

sentences.zh: 至是，純仁薦為永興軍路鈐轄，又薦知隰州。

translations.literal: At this time, Chunren recommended him as Yongxing Circuit military controller, then recommended him as prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chunren recommended him as Yongxing Circuit military controller, then as prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 每自咎曰：「先人與種氏上世有契義，純仁不肖，為其子孫所訟，甯論曲直哉。」

translations.literal: He often blamed himself, saying: "My forebears and the Zhong clan's forebears had sworn fellowship in former generations. Chunren is unworthy, yet sued by their descendants—how can I weigh right and wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: He often reproached himself: "My ancestors and the Zhong clan's forebears were bound by sworn fellowship. I am a poor son, yet their descendants sued me—how can I argue over right and wrong?"

sentences.zh: 元祐初，進吏部尚書，數日，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou, he was promoted to Minister of Personnel; within days, made Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he was promoted to Minister of Personnel; within days he was made associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，純仁與議西夏，請罷兵棄地，使歸所掠漢人，執政持之未決。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chunren had debated Western Xia policy, urging cessation of war and surrender of territory, and return of captured Han people—the chief ministers withheld judgment and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chunren had argued over Western Xia policy, urging peace, cession of territory, and return of captured Han subjects. The chief ministers had not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃申前議，又請歸一漢人予十縑。

translations.literal: At this time he reasserted his former proposal, also requesting ten bolts of silk for each Han person returned.
translations.idiomatic: Now he renewed his earlier proposal and also asked that ten bolts of silk be paid for each Han captive returned.

sentences.zh: 事皆施行。

translations.literal: All measures were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All were carried out.

sentences.zh: 邊俘鬼章以獻，純仁請誅之塞上，以謝邊人，不聽。

translations.literal: A frontier captive, Gui Zhang, was presented as tribute. Chunren requested execution on the border to appease frontier people—he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The captive chief Gui Zhang was brought in as tribute. Chunren asked that he be executed on the frontier to satisfy the border people. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 議者欲致其子，收河南故地，故赦不殺。

translations.literal: Advocates wished to bring his son and recover old Henan territory, therefore pardoned him and did not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Some hoped to lure his son and recover old Henan territory, so Gui Zhang was spared.

sentences.zh: 後又欲官之，純仁復固爭，然鬼章子卒不至。

translations.literal: Later they again wished to give him office; Chunren again firmly objected, yet Gui Zhang's son never came in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court wanted to appoint Gui Zhang to office. Chunren objected again—but Gui Zhang's son never arrived.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 純仁在位，務以博大開上意，忠篤革士風。

translations.literal: While Chunren held office, he devoted himself to broad magnanimity to open the sovereign's mind, and sincerity and faithfulness to reform the spirit of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In office Chunren sought to broaden the emperor's outlook with magnanimity and reform scholarly morals with steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 章惇得罪去，朝廷以其父老，欲畀便郡，既而中止。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun, having offended, departed; the court, considering his father aged, wished to give him a convenient prefecture, but then halted the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun, having fallen from grace, was leaving court. Because his father was elderly, the court considered giving him a comfortable provincial post—but then dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 純仁請置往咎而念其私情。

translations.literal: Chunren requested setting aside past blame and considering his private feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren asked that past offenses be set aside out of regard for Zhang Dun's family ties.

sentences.zh: 鄧綰帥淮東，言者斥之不已。

translations.literal: Deng Wan commanded Huaidong; remonstrators attacked him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan commanded Huaidong, and critics attacked him relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「臣嘗為綰誣奏坐黜，今日所陳為綰也，左降不宜錄人之過太深。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Your servant was once falsely memorialized against by Wan and demoted. What is said today targets Wan. In demotion one should not record a man's faults too deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Wan once memorialized falsely against me and got me demoted. Today's attacks target him. In demotion one should not dwell too deeply on a man's faults.

sentences.zh: 」宣仁後嘉納。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager Xuanren praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Empress Dowager Xuanren approved.

sentences.zh: 因下詔：「前日希合附會之人，一無所問。」

translations.literal: Therefore an edict was issued: "Those who formerly sought favor and attached themselves—none shall be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Those who once sought favor by joining factions will face no inquiries."

sentences.zh: 學士蘇軾以發策問為言者所攻，韓維無名罷門下侍郎補外。

translations.literal: Academician Su Shi was attacked by remonstrators for his palace-examination policy questions; Han Wei, without stated cause, was dismissed from Vice Director of the Chancellery and sent out to a provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Su Shi was attacked over his palace-examination policy questions. Han Wei was removed as Vice Director of the Chancellery without stated cause and sent to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 純仁奏軾無罪，維盡心國家，不可因譖黜官。

translations.literal: Chunren memorialized that Shi was without guilt and Wei devoted himself utterly to the state—they could not be dismissed on account of slander.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren memorialized that Su Shi was innocent and Han Wei had served the state wholeheartedly—they should not be removed on the strength of slander.

sentences.zh: 及王覿言事忤旨，純仁慮朋黨將熾，與文彥博、呂公著辨於簾前，未解。

translations.literal: When Wang Di spoke on affairs contrary to the imperial will, Chunren feared factions would blaze up; with Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongzhu he argued before the curtain, without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Di spoke against the imperial will, Chunren feared factionalism would flare up. He argued before the regent with Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongzhu, but the dispute remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「朝臣本無黨，但善惡邪正，各以類分。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Court officials originally have no factions—it is only that good and evil, crooked and straight, each group by kind.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "There are no factions at court as such—only men sorted by what is good or evil, straight or crooked.

sentences.zh: 彥博、公著皆累朝舊人，豈容雷同罔上。

translations.literal: Yanbo and Gongzhu are both officials of many reigns—how could they be permitted to echo one another and deceive the sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and Gongzhu are veterans of many reigns. How could they simply echo one another and deceive the throne?

sentences.zh: 昔先臣與韓琦、富弼同慶曆柄任，各舉所知，常時飛語指為朋黨，三人相繼補外，造謗者公相慶曰一綱打盡，此事未遠，願陛下戒之。

translations.literal: In the past my late father together with Han Qi and Fu Bi shared power in the Qingli era, each recommending those he knew. At the time flying slander called them a faction; the three were sent out to provincial posts in succession, and the slanderers openly rejoiced saying the whole net had been drawn in. This is not distant—I hope Your Majesty will take warning.
translations.idiomatic: My late father once shared power with Han Qi and Fu Bi in the Qingli era, each recommending men he knew. Rumor called them a faction. All three were sent to the provinces in turn, and slanderers openly rejoiced that the net had caught every fish. That was not long ago. I pray Your Majesty will heed the warning.

sentences.zh: 」因極言前世朋黨之禍，並錄歐陽修《朋黨論》以進。

translations.literal: " He then spoke at length on the calamities of factions in former ages, and copied Ouyang Xiu's "On Factions" to present.
translations.idiomatic: " He then spoke at length on the disasters of factionalism in earlier ages and submitted a copy of Ouyang Xiu's On Factions.

sentences.zh: 知漢陽軍吳處厚傅致蔡確安州《車蓋亭詩》，以為謗宣仁后，上之。

translations.literal: Wu Chuhou, prefect of Hanyang, transmitted and brought Cai Que's Anzhou "Carriage-Pavilion Poems," taking them as slandering Empress Dowager Xuanren, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chuhou, prefect of Hanyang, forwarded Cai Que's Carriage-Pavilion poems from Anzhou, claiming they slandered Empress Dowager Xuanren, and submitted them to court.

sentences.zh: 諫官欲寘於典憲，執政右其說，唯純仁與左丞王存以為不可。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials wished to punish under the penal code; the chief ministers supported their view—only Chunren and Left Vice Director Wang Cun thought it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials wanted to prosecute under the penal code. The chief ministers agreed. Only Chunren and Left Vice Director Wang Cun objected.

sentences.zh: 爭之未定，聞太師文彥博欲貶於嶺嶠，純仁謂左相呂大防曰：「此路自乾興以來，荊棘近七十年，吾輩開之，恐自不免。

translations.literal: While the dispute was undecided, he heard Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo wished to banish him to the southern mountains. Chunren said to Left Chief Minister Lü Dafang: "This path since Qianxing has been thorny for nearly seventy years. If we open it, I fear we ourselves will not escape.
translations.idiomatic: While the debate continued, Chunren heard that Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo wanted to banish Cai Que to the far south. He told Left Chief Minister Lü Dafang, "That road has been overgrown with thorns since the Qianxing era—nearly seventy years. If we open it, I fear we will not escape it ourselves.

sentences.zh: 」大防遂不敢言。

translations.literal: " Dafang then did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Dafang then fell silent.

sentences.zh: 及確新州命下，純仁于宣仁后簾前言：「聖朝宜務寬厚，不可以語言文字之間曖昧不明之過，誅竄大臣。

translations.literal: When Que's assignment to Xinzhou was issued, Chunren spoke before Empress Dowager Xuanren behind the curtain: "The holy dynasty should devote itself to magnanimity. One cannot on account of ambiguous and unclear faults in words and writing execute and banish great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Que's exile to Xinzhou was ordered, Chunren spoke before the regent: "Our dynasty should hold to magnanimity. One must not banish great ministers over ambiguous turns of phrase in a poem or essay.

sentences.zh: 今舉動宜與將來為法，此事甚不可開端也。

translations.literal: Today's actions should serve as law for the future—this matter must not be opened as a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: What the court does now will become precedent for the future. This must not be the start of such a path.

sentences.zh: 且以重刑除惡，如以猛藥治病，其過也，不能無損焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, using heavy punishment to remove evil is like using fierce medicine to treat illness—even when it goes too far, harm cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Using harsh punishment to root out evil is like treating illness with fierce medicine: even when necessary, some harm cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 」又與王存諫于哲宗，退而上疏，其略云：「蓋如父母之有逆子，雖天地鬼神不能容貸，父子至親，主於恕而已。

translations.literal: " He also remonstrated together with Wang Cun before Zhezong; withdrawing he submitted a memorial, the gist of which was: "It is like parents with a rebellious son—though Heaven and Earth and spirits cannot pardon him, yet in the closest bond of father and son, what governs is forgiveness alone.
translations.idiomatic: " He and Wang Cun remonstrated before Zhezong, then Chunren withdrew and memorialized in essence: "It is like parents with a rebellious son. Even Heaven and Earth cannot pardon him—and yet between father and son, what governs above all is forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 若處之必死之地，則恐傷恩。

translations.literal: If one places him in ground where death is certain, then I fear kinship affection will be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: To place him where death is certain would wound that bond of grace.

sentences.zh: 」確卒貶新州。

translations.literal: " Que was finally banished to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Cai Que was banished to Xinzhou after all.

sentences.zh: 大防奏確黨人甚盛，不可不問。

translations.literal: Dafang memorialized that Que's faction was very strong and could not go uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafang memorialized that Cai Que's faction was too powerful to ignore.

sentences.zh: 純仁面諫朋黨難辨，恐誤及善人。

translations.literal: Chunren remonstrated in person that factions are hard to distinguish, fearing the good would be wrongly implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren remonstrated in person that factions are hard to distinguish and that good men might be swept up by mistake.

sentences.zh: 遂上疏曰：「朋黨之起，蓋因趣向異同，同我者謂之正人，異我者疑為邪黨。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "Factions arise because inclinations differ and align: those who agree with me are called upright men; those who differ from me are suspected as an evil faction.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Factions arise because men sort themselves by inclination. Those who agree with me are called upright; those who differ are suspected of forming an evil clique.

sentences.zh: 既惡其異我，則逆耳之言難至；

translations.literal: Once one hates those who differ from me, then unwelcome words hardly arrive;
translations.idiomatic: Once you resent those who disagree, unwelcome counsel rarely reaches you;

sentences.zh: 既喜其同我，則迎合之佞日親。

translations.literal: once one delights in those who agree with me, then flatterers who accommodate draw daily closer.
translations.idiomatic: once you delight in agreement, sycophants who tell you what you want to hear draw daily closer.

sentences.zh: 以至真偽莫知，賢愚倒置，國家之患，率由此也。

translations.literal: Thus truth and falsehood are unknown, worthy and foolish reversed—the state's calamities mostly arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and falsehood blur, worthy and foolish are reversed—the state's gravest troubles mostly begin here.

sentences.zh: 至如王安石，正因喜同惡異，遂至黑白不分，至今風俗，猶以觀望為能，後來柄臣，固合永為商鑒。

translations.literal: Take Wang Anshi: precisely because he delighted in agreement and hated difference, black and white became indistinguishable. To this day custom still treats hesitation as ability—later power-holders should forever take this as a warning mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi is the example: delighting in agreement and hating dissent, he left truth and falsehood indistinguishable. Even now the habit of fence-sitting passes for wisdom. Later power-holders should take this as an everlasting warning.

sentences.zh: 今蔡確不必推治黨人，旁及枝葉。

translations.literal: Now with Cai Que there is no need to extend investigation of factions to branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to pursue Cai Que's faction to every branch and leaf.

sentences.zh: 臣聞孔子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard Confucius say: 'Raise the upright and set them over the crooked, and the crooked can be made straight.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Raise the upright and set them over the crooked, and the crooked will be made straight.

sentences.zh: 』則是舉用正直，而可以化枉邪為善人，不仁者自當屏跡矣。

translations.literal: ' Then by elevating and employing the upright, one can transform the crooked and evil into good men; the unkind will naturally withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Elevate the upright, and the crooked may become good. The unprincipled will withdraw of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 何煩分辨黨人，或恐有傷仁化。

translations.literal: Why trouble to distinguish faction members? Perhaps fearing harm to benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Why bother sorting out factions at all—and risk damaging the cultivation of benevolence?

sentences.zh: 」司諫吳安詩、正言劉安世交章擊純仁黨確，純仁亦力求罷。

translations.literal: " Supervising remonstrator Wu Anshi and rectifier Liu Anshi submitted memorials in succession attacking Chunren as Que's partisan; Chunren also forcefully sought dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising remonstrator Wu Anshi and rectifier Liu Anshi memorialized in succession that Chunren was Cai Que's partisan. Chunren also pressed hard to resign.

sentences.zh: 明年，以觀文殿學士知潁昌府。

translations.literal: The next year, as Hanlin academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature he was made prefect of Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Hanlin academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加大學士、知太原府。

translations.literal: After a year, he was given grand academician rank and made prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made grand academician and prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其境土狹民眾，惜地不葬。

translations.literal: That circuit's land was narrow and population dense; people begrudged land for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The territory was cramped and populous; people hoarded land and would not bury their dead.

sentences.zh: 純仁遣僚屬收無主燼骨，別男女異穴，葬者三千餘。

translations.literal: Chunren sent subordinates to gather ownerless cremated bones, separating men and women into different graves; more than three thousand were buried.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren sent staff to collect unclaimed cremated remains, burying men and women in separate graves—more than three thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 又推之一路，葬以萬數計。

translations.literal: He extended this across the circuit; burials numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He extended the practice across the circuit; burials numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯境，朝廷欲罪將吏。

translations.literal: Tangut people violated the border; the court wished to punish commanders and officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanguts raided the border, the court wanted to punish the commanders.

sentences.zh: 純仁自引咎求貶。

translations.literal: Chunren took blame upon himself and sought demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren accepted blame and asked to be demoted.

sentences.zh: 秋，有詔貶官一等，徙河南府，再徙潁昌。

translations.literal: In autumn, an edict demoted him one rank and transferred him to Henan prefecture, then again to Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn an edict demoted him one rank, sent him to Henan prefecture, then to Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 召還，復拜右僕射。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was again appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was again made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 因入謝，宣仁后簾中諭曰：「或謂卿必先引用王覿、彭汝礪，卿宜與呂大防一心。

translations.literal: On entering to give thanks, Empress Dowager Xuanren instructed behind the curtain: "Some say you must first promote Wang Di and Peng Rulü—you should be of one mind with Lü Dafang.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to give thanks, the regent said from behind the curtain, "Some say you will promote Wang Di and Peng Rulü first. You should stand with Lü Dafang as one.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此二人實有士望，臣終不敢保位蔽賢，望陛下加察。

translations.literal: " He replied: "These two men truly enjoy scholarly reputation. Your servant would never dare keep his post and block the worthy—I hope Your Majesty will examine further.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Both men truly enjoy scholarly reputation. I would never cling to office and block the worthy. I pray Your Majesty will look into this.

sentences.zh: 」純仁將再入也，楊畏不悅，嘗有言，純仁不知。

translations.literal: " As Chunren was about to enter office again, Yang Wei was displeased and had once spoken of it—Chunren did not know.
translations.idiomatic: " As Chunren was about to return to office, Yang Wei was displeased and had spoken against him—but Chunren did not know.

sentences.zh: 至是，大防約畏為助，欲引為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At this time, Dafang enlisted Wei as helper and wished to bring him in as Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lü Dafang enlisted Yang Wei as an ally and wanted to appoint him Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「諫官當用正人，畏不可用。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Remonstrance officials should employ upright men—Wei cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Remonstrance officials must be upright men. Yang Wei is unfit.

sentences.zh: 」大防曰：「豈以畏嘗言公邪？

translations.literal: " Dafang said: "Is it because Wei once spoke of you?
translations.idiomatic: " Dafang asked, "Is this because Wei once spoke against you?

sentences.zh: 」純仁始知之。

translations.literal: " Chunren only then learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then did Chunren learn of it.

sentences.zh: 後畏叛大防，凡有以害大防者，無所不至。

translations.literal: Later Wei betrayed Dafang; whatever could harm Dafang, he did without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Wei turned on Lü Dafang and stopped at nothing to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 宣仁後寢疾，召純仁曰：「卿父仲淹，可謂忠臣。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren fell ill; summoning Chunren she said: "Your father Zhongyan may be called a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the regent fell ill, she summoned Chunren and said, "Your father Zhongyan was a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 在明肅皇后垂簾時，唯勸明肅盡母道；

translations.literal: When Empress Mingsu held the curtain, he only urged Mingsu to fulfill the way of a mother;
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Mingsu was regent, he urged her only to fulfill a mother's duty;

sentences.zh: 明肅上賓，唯勸仁宗盡子道。

translations.literal: when Mingsu ascended to be guest of Heaven, he only urged Renzong to fulfill the way of a son.
translations.idiomatic: when she passed away, he urged Renzong only to fulfill a son's duty.

sentences.zh: 卿當似之。

translations.literal: You should be like him.
translations.idiomatic: You should be like him.

sentences.zh: 」純仁泣曰：「敢不盡忠。

translations.literal: " Chunren wept and said: "How dare I not devote myself in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren wept and said, "How could I fail to serve with full loyalty?

sentences.zh: 宣仁后崩，哲宗親政，純仁乞避位。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanren died, Zhezong personally governed; Chunren requested to step aside.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xuanren died and Zhezong took power himself, Chunren asked to step down.

sentences.zh: 哲宗語呂大防曰：「純仁有時望，不宜去，可為朕留之。

translations.literal: Zhezong told Lü Dafang: "Chunren enjoys contemporary esteem; he should not leave—you may keep him for me.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong told Lü Dafang, "Chunren enjoys great public standing. He should not go. Keep him for me.

sentences.zh: 」且趣入見，問：「先朝行青苗法如何？

translations.literal: " And urged him to enter audience, asking: "How was the green-sprouts law of the former reign?
translations.idiomatic: " He was summoned at once and asked, "What do you think of the green-sprouts policy of the previous reign?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「先帝愛民之意本深，但王安石立法過甚，激以賞罰，故官吏急切，以致害民。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The former emperor's intent to love the people was originally deep, but Wang Anshi's legislation was excessive; spurred by rewards and punishments, officials became urgent, thereby harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "The late emperor's care for the people was genuine. But Wang Anshi's laws went too far. Driven by rewards and punishments, officials grew frantic—and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 」退而上疏，其要以為「青苗非所當行，行之終不免擾民也」。

translations.literal: " Withdrawing he submitted a memorial, its gist being that "green sprouts ought not to be implemented; implementing it will ultimately fail to avoid disturbing the people."
translations.idiomatic: " Withdrawing, he memorialized in essence that "the green-sprouts policy should not be pursued; pursued to the end, it will only disturb the people."

sentences.zh: 是時，用二三大臣，皆從中出，侍從、臺諫官，亦多不由進擬。

translations.literal: At this time, appointing two or three great ministers—all came from the inner palace; attendant officials and censor-remonstrators too mostly were not through regular nomination.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the two or three chief ministers were all appointed from within the palace. Attendants and censor-remonstrators too were often chosen without regular nomination.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「陛下初親政，四方拭目以觀，天下治亂，實本於此。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Your Majesty has just personally governed; the four quarters wipe their eyes to watch—the realm's order and disorder truly root in this.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Your Majesty has just taken power. All the realm watches with clear eyes. Whether the state thrives or fails begins here.

sentences.zh: 舜舉皋陶，湯舉伊尹，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Shun raised Gao Yao; Tang raised Yi Yin—the unkind withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shun raised Gao Yao, Tang raised Yi Yin—and the unprincipled withdrew.

sentences.zh: 縱未能如古人，亦須極天下之選。

translations.literal: Even if one cannot be like the ancients, one must still exhaust the realm's choices.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty cannot match the ancients, choose from the best the realm has to offer.

sentences.zh: 」又群小力排宣仁后垂簾時事，純仁奏曰：「太皇保佑聖躬，功烈誠心，幽明共監，議者不恤國事，一何薄哉。

translations.literal: " Again petty men forcefully rejected matters from Empress Dowager Xuanren's regency. Chunren memorialized: "The Grand Empress Dowager protected the sacred person; her achievements and sincere heart are witnessed by the hidden and the manifest—those who debate show no care for state affairs. How shallow!
translations.idiomatic: " Petty men meanwhile assailed every policy of the regency. Chunren memorialized, "The Grand Empress Dowager guarded the throne with sincere devotion, witnessed in this world and the next. Critics who ignore the good of the state—how shallow they are!

sentences.zh: 」遂以仁宗禁言明肅垂簾事詔書上之。

translations.literal: " He then submitted the edict from Renzong forbidding discussion of Empress Mingsu's regency.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted Renzong's edict forbidding discussion of Empress Mingsu's regency.

sentences.zh: 曰：「望陛下稽仿而行，以戒薄俗。」

translations.literal: Saying: "I hope Your Majesty will examine and imitate it in practice, to warn against shallow custom."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, "I pray Your Majesty will follow that precedent and curb this shallow custom."

sentences.zh: 蘇轍論殿試策問，引漢昭變武帝法度事。

translations.literal: Su Zhe in discussion of palace-examination policy questions cited Emperor Zhao of Han changing Emperor Wu's laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In a palace-examination policy question, Su Zhe cited how Emperor Zhao of Han had altered Emperor Wu's institutions.

sentences.zh: 哲宗震怒曰：「安得以漢武比先帝？

translations.literal: Zhezong enraged said: "How can Han Wu be compared to the former emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong erupted in anger. "How dare you compare Emperor Wu to the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 」轍下殿待罪，眾不敢仰視。

translations.literal: " Zhe left the hall to await punishment; the assembly dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Zhe stepped down to await punishment. No one in the hall dared look up.

sentences.zh: 純仁從容言：「武帝雄才大略，史無貶辭。

translations.literal: Chunren calmly said: "Emperor Wu had heroic talent and great design—history has no words of condemnation.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said calmly, "Emperor Wu was a man of heroic vision and great design. History does not condemn him.

sentences.zh: 轍以比先帝，非謗也。

translations.literal: Zhe compared him to the former emperor—this is not slander.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe compared him to the late emperor. That is not slander.

sentences.zh: 陛下親事之始，進退大臣，不當如訶叱奴僕。

translations.literal: At the start of Your Majesty's personal governance, advancing and dismissing great ministers should not be like scolding bondservants.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Your personal rule, advancing and dismissing great ministers should not be like berating a servant.

sentences.zh: 」右丞鄧潤甫越次曰：「先帝法度，為司馬光、蘇轍壞盡。

translations.literal: " Right Vice Director Deng Runfu overstepping his order said: "The former emperor's laws and institutions have been ruined entirely by Sima Guang and Su Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: " Right Vice Director Deng Runfu interrupted: "Sima Guang and Su Zhe have ruined the late emperor's entire legacy of law.

sentences.zh: 」純仁曰：「不然，法本無弊，弊則當改。

translations.literal: " Chunren said: "Not so. Law originally has no flaw; where there is flaw, it should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren said, "Not so. Law itself is not flawed. Where it is flawed, it should be changed.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗曰：「人謂秦皇、漢武。

translations.literal: " Zhezong said: "People speak of Qin Shi Huang and Han Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezong said, "People compare him to Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 」純仁曰：「轍所論，事與時也，非人也。

translations.literal: " Chunren said: "What Zhe discussed concerns affairs and the age—not the person.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren said, "Su Zhe spoke of policies and their times—not of the man himself.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗為之少霽。

translations.literal: " Zhezong for this grew somewhat clear.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezong's anger eased a little.

sentences.zh: 轍平日與純仁多異，至是乃服謝純仁曰：「公佛地位中人也。

translations.literal: Zhe on ordinary days differed greatly from Chunren; at this he submitted and thanked Chunren, saying: "Sir, you are a man at the Buddha's level.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe often disagreed with Chunren—but now he bowed and thanked him, saying, "You are a man of Buddha's stature.

sentences.zh: 」轍竟落職知汝州。

translations.literal: " Zhe ultimately lost office and was made prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Zhe was still stripped of office and sent to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 全台言蘇軾行呂惠卿告詞，訕謗先帝，黜知英州。

translations.literal: The entire censorate said Su Shi, drafting Lü Huiqing's farewell rescript, slandered the former emperor; he was demoted to prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The entire censorate charged that Su Shi's draft of Lü Huiqing's farewell rescript slandered the late emperor. He was demoted to prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 純仁上疏曰：「熙甯法度，皆惠卿附會王安石建議，不副先帝愛民求治之意。

translations.literal: Chunren submitted a memorial saying: "The Xining laws and institutions were all built on Huiqing's attaching himself to Wang Anshi's proposals—they did not accord with the former emperor's intent to love the people and seek good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren memorialized, "The Xining reforms were Lü Huiqing's work, attached to Wang Anshi's proposals. They did not match the late emperor's intent to love the people and govern well.

sentences.zh: 至垂簾之際，始用言者，特行貶竄，今已八年矣。

translations.literal: Only when the regency began were remonstrators heeded, and special banishments were carried out. Eight years have passed since then.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the regency began did the court heed remonstrators and carry out special banishments—and eight years have passed since then.

sentences.zh: 言者多當時御史，何故畏避不即納忠，今乃有是奏，豈非觀望邪？

translations.literal: Most of those remonstrators were censors at the time. Why did they hold back and not offer loyal counsel immediately? That they submit such a memorial only now—is this not watching which way the wind blows?
translations.idiomatic: Most of those critics were censors at the time. Why did they hold back and not speak up then? That they submit such a memorial only now—surely they are waiting to see which way the wind blows.

sentences.zh: 」御史來之邵言高士敦任成都鈐轄日不法事，及蘇轍所謫太近。

translations.literal: " Censor Lai Zhishao reported Gao Shidun's unlawful conduct while military controller at Chengdu, and that Su Zhe's demotion was too lenient.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor Lai Zhishao reported unlawful conduct by Gao Shidun while he was military controller at Chengdu, and charged that Su Zhe's demotion was too lenient.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「之邵為成都監司，士敦有犯，自當按發。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Zhishao was Chengdu's surveillance commissioner. If Shidun had offenses, he ought to have been investigated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Zhishao was the surveillance commissioner at Chengdu. If Shidun had broken the law, Zhishao should have investigated him then.

sentences.zh: 轍與政累年，之邵已作御史，亦無糾正，今乃繼有二奏，其情可知。」

translations.literal: Su Zhe held office for years while Zhishao was already a censor, yet there was no correction. Now there are two memorials in succession—the motive is clear."
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe held office for years while Zhishao was already a censor, yet he never corrected him. Now there are two memorials in a row—the motive is plain."

sentences.zh: 純仁凡薦引人材，必以天下公議，其人不知自純仁所出。

translations.literal: In recommending talent, Chunren always relied on public consensus throughout the realm; those he recommended did not know the recommendation came from him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chunren recommended talent, he relied on public consensus across the realm. Those he advanced never knew the recommendation came from him.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「為宰相，豈可不牢籠天下士，使知出於門下？

translations.literal: Someone said: "As chancellor, should you not bind scholars throughout the realm to yourself, so they know they owe their advancement to your patronage?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "As chancellor, should you not bind scholars across the realm to yourself, so they know they owe their advancement to your patronage?

sentences.zh: 」純仁曰：'但朝廷進用不失正人，何必知出於我邪？

translations.literal: " Chunren said, "So long as the court appoints upright men, why must they know it came from me?
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren replied, "So long as the court appoints upright men, why must they know the recommendation came from me?

sentences.zh: 」哲宗既召章惇為相，純仁堅請去，遂以觀文殿大學士加右正議大夫知潁昌府。

translations.literal: " After Zhezong summoned Zhang Dun as chancellor, Chunren firmly asked to leave office. He was made grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature with the added title Right Rectifier Grand Master and prefect of Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: " After Zhezong summoned Zhang Dun as chancellor, Chunren pressed hard to resign. He was made grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, with the added title Right Rectifier Grand Master, and prefect of Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 入辭，哲宗曰：「卿不肯為朕留，雖在外，于時政有見，宜悉以聞，毋事形跡。

translations.literal: On taking leave, Zhezong said: "Since you will not stay for me, though you are in the provinces, if you have views on current affairs you should report them all to me—do not stand on ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to bid farewell, Zhezong said, "Since you will not stay for me, though you serve in the provinces, report whatever you see of current affairs—do not stand on ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」徙河南府，又徙陳州。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Henan prefecture, then to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Henan prefecture, then to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，哲宗嘗言：「貶謫之人，殆似永廢。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhezong had once said: "Men who are demoted and banished are all but permanently cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhezong had once said, "Men who are demoted and banished are all but cast aside forever.

sentences.zh: 」純仁前賀曰：「陛下念及此，堯、舜用心也。」

translations.literal: " Chunren stepped forward to congratulate him: "Your Majesty's concern for this shows the mind of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren stepped forward to congratulate him: "Your Majesty's concern for this shows the mind of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 既而呂大防等竄嶺表，會明堂肆赦，章惇先期言：「此數十人，當終身勿徙。

translations.literal: Soon Lü Dafang and others were banished to the southern mountains. When a general amnesty was held at the Bright Hall, Zhang Dun said in advance: "These several dozen men should never be moved for their entire lives.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lü Dafang and others were banished to the far south. When a general amnesty was proclaimed at the Bright Hall, Zhang Dun said in advance, "These several dozen men should never be moved for the rest of their lives.

sentences.zh: 」純仁聞而憂憤，欲齋戒上疏申理之。

translations.literal: " Chunren, hearing this, grew anxious and angry and wished to fast and submit a memorial pleading their case.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren, hearing this, grew anxious and angry and wished to fast and submit a memorial in their defense.

sentences.zh: 所親勸以勿為觸怒，萬一遠斥，非高年所宜。

translations.literal: Those close to him urged him not to provoke anger—for at his advanced age, banishment to a distant place would be unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Those close to him urged him not to provoke anger—for at his age, banishment to a distant place would be too much to bear.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「事至於此，無一人敢言，若上心遂回，所系大矣。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Matters have come to this and no one dares speak. If the sovereign's mind is truly turned, what hangs in the balance is enormous.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Matters have come to this and no one dares speak. If the sovereign's mind is truly turned, what hangs in the balance is enormous.

sentences.zh: 不然，死亦何憾。

translations.literal: Otherwise, what regret would death hold?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, what regret would death hold?

sentences.zh: 」乃疏曰：「大防等年老疾病，不習水土，炎荒非久處之地，又憂虞不測，何以自存。

translations.literal: " He memorialized: "Dafang and the others are old and ill, unaccustomed to local climates; the hot wastes are no place to dwell long, and they also fear unforeseen danger—how can they preserve themselves?
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized, "Dafang and the others are old and ill, unaccustomed to local climates. The hot wastes are no place to dwell long, and they also fear unforeseen danger—how can they survive?

sentences.zh: 臣曾與大防等共事，多被排斥，陛下之所親見。

translations.literal: Your servant once served with Dafang and the others and was often cast aside—Your Majesty saw this yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once served with Dafang and the others and was often cast aside—Your Majesty saw this yourself.

sentences.zh: 臣之激切，止是仰報聖德。

translations.literal: My urgency is only to repay Your Majesty's sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: My urgency is only to repay Your Majesty's sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 向來章惇、呂惠卿雖為貶謫，不出裏居。

translations.literal: In the past, though Zhang Dun and Lü Huiqing were demoted and banished, they were not sent beyond residence in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, though Zhang Dun and Lü Huiqing were demoted and banished, they were not sent beyond residence in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 臣向曾有言，深蒙陛下開納，陛下以一蔡確之故，常軫聖念。

translations.literal: Your servant spoke on this before and was deeply received by Your Majesty's openness. Because of one Cai Que, Your Majesty has often shown tender concern.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant spoke on this before and was deeply received by Your Majesty's openness. Because of one Cai Que, Your Majesty has often shown tender concern.

sentences.zh: 今赴彥若已死貶所，將不止一蔡確矣。

translations.literal: Now Fu Yanruo has died in his place of banishment—it will not stop with one Cai Que.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fu Yanruo has died in his place of banishment—it will not stop with one Cai Que.

sentences.zh: 願陛下斷自淵衷，將大防等引赦原放。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will decide from the depths of your heart and bring Dafang and the others within the amnesty and release them.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will decide from the depths of your heart and bring Dafang and the others within the amnesty and release them.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，忤惇意，詆為同罪，落職知隨州。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, it offended Zhang Dun. Chunren was denounced as sharing their guilt, demoted from office, and made prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, it offended Zhang Dun. Chunren was denounced as sharing their guilt, stripped of office, and made prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，又貶武安軍節度副使、永州安置。

translations.literal: The next year he was further demoted to military vice commissioner of Wu'an Army and placed under restraint at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was further demoted to military vice commissioner of Wu'an Army and placed under restraint at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時疾失明，聞命怡然就道。

translations.literal: By then illness had blinded him; hearing the order, he set out on the road with equanimity.
translations.idiomatic: By then illness had blinded him. Hearing the order, he set out on the road with equanimity.

sentences.zh: 或謂近名，純仁曰：「七十之年，兩目俱喪，萬里之行，豈其欲哉？

translations.literal: Some said he sought fame. Chunren said: "At seventy, with both eyes gone—a journey of ten thousand li—is that what I would choose?
translations.idiomatic: Some said he sought fame. Chunren said, "At seventy, with both eyes gone—a journey of ten thousand li—is that what I would choose?

sentences.zh: 但區區之愛君，有懷不盡，若避好名之嫌，則無為善之路矣。

translations.literal: It is only my slight love for the sovereign, with feelings I cannot fully express. If I shunned the suspicion of seeking fame, there would be no path left for doing good.
translations.idiomatic: It is only my slight love for the sovereign, with feelings I cannot fully express. If I shunned the suspicion of seeking fame, there would be no path left for doing good.

sentences.zh: 」每戒子弟毋得小有不平，聞諸子怨章惇，純仁必怒止之。

translations.literal: " He constantly warned his sons and grandsons not to harbor the slightest resentment. When he heard his sons grumbling about Zhang Dun, Chunren always stopped them angrily.
translations.idiomatic: " He constantly warned his sons and grandsons not to harbor the slightest resentment. When he heard his sons grumbling about Zhang Dun, Chunren always stopped them angrily.

sentences.zh: 江行赴貶所，舟覆，扶純仁出，衣盡濕。

translations.literal: Traveling by river to his place of banishment, the boat capsized. They pulled Chunren out, his clothes soaked through.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling by river to his place of banishment, the boat capsized. They pulled Chunren out, his clothes soaked through.

sentences.zh: 顧諸子曰：「此豈章惇為之哉？

translations.literal: He turned to his sons and said: "Surely Zhang Dun did not cause this?
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his sons and said, "Surely Zhang Dun did not cause this?

sentences.zh: 」既至永，韓維責均州，其子訴維執政日與司馬光不合，得免行。

translations.literal: " After reaching Yong, Han Wei was assigned to Junzhou. His son appealed that during Wei's time in power he had disagreed with Sima Guang, and Wei was exempted from going.
translations.idiomatic: " After reaching Yong, Han Wei was assigned to Junzhou. His son appealed that during Wei's time in power he had disagreed with Sima Guang, and Wei was exempted from going.

sentences.zh: 純仁之子欲以純仁與光議役法不同為請，純仁曰：「吾用君實薦，以至宰相。

translations.literal: Chunren's son wanted to appeal on the ground that Chunren and Guang had disagreed on the labor-service law. Chunren said: "It was through Junshi's recommendation that I reached the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren's son wanted to appeal on the ground that Chunren and Guang had disagreed on the labor-service law. Chunren said, "It was through Junshi's recommendation that I reached the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 昔同朝論事不合則可，汝輩以為今日之言，則不可也。

translations.literal: In the past, when we served together in court, disagreement on policy was acceptable—but you must not use that as grounds for appeal today.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when we served together in court, disagreement on policy was acceptable—but you must not use that as grounds for appeal today.

sentences.zh: 有愧心而生者，不若無愧心而死。

translations.literal: Better to die without a guilty conscience than to live with one.
translations.idiomatic: Better to die without a guilty conscience than to live with one.

sentences.zh: 」其子乃止。

translations.literal: " His son then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " His son then desisted.

sentences.zh: 居三年，徽宗即位，欽聖顯肅後同聽政，即日授純仁光祿卿，分司南京，鄧州居住。

translations.literal: After three years, Huizong ascended the throne. Empress Dowager Qinsheng jointly administered affairs with him and that same day appointed Chunren Gentleman of the Bright Hall, with nominal duty at the Southern Capital and residence at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, Huizong ascended the throne. Empress Dowager Qinsheng jointly administered affairs with him and that same day appointed Chunren Gentleman of the Bright Hall, with nominal duty at the Southern Capital and residence at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣中使至永賜茶藥，諭曰：「皇帝在藩邸，太皇太后在宮中，知公先朝言事忠直，今虛相位以待，不知目疾如何，用何人醫之。

translations.literal: A palace envoy was sent to Yong with tea and medicine, conveying: "When the emperor was still in his princely residence and the Grand Empress Dowager was in the palace, they knew of your loyal and forthright remonstrance in the previous reign. The chancellorship is now left vacant awaiting you. We do not know how your eye ailment is—what physician do you use?
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy was sent to Yong with tea and medicine, conveying, "When the emperor was still in his princely residence and the Grand Empress Dowager was in the palace, they knew of your loyal and forthright remonstrance in the previous reign. The chancellorship is now left vacant awaiting you. We do not know how your eye ailment is—what physician do you use?

sentences.zh: 」純仁頓首謝。

translations.literal: " Chunren kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 道除右正議大夫、提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: En route he was appointed Right Rectifier Grand Master and superintendent of the Palace of Extending Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: En route he was appointed Right Rectifier Grand Master and superintendent of the Palace of Extending Blessings.

sentences.zh: 不數月，以觀文殿大學士、中太一宮使詔之。

translations.literal: Within months he was summoned as grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and director of the Central Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was summoned as grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and director of the Central Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 有曰：「豈唯尊德尚齒，昭示寵優；

translations.literal: The rescript read in part: "Is this not only to honor virtue and respect age, making favor clear to all;
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read in part, "Is this not only to honor virtue and respect age, making favor clear to all;

sentences.zh: 庶幾鯁論嘉謀，日聞忠告。

translations.literal: but also so that forthright counsel and excellent plans may daily reach the throne?
